definition_zh: 蛋白质；由氨基酸链折叠成特定形状的生物大分子；膳食中提供氨基酸的营养成分
definition_en: a large molecule built from a chain of amino acids and folded into a working shape, and by extension the nutrient class that supplies such molecules
core_image: 一串彩色珠子被揉成一团，表面有凹槽与凸起，正好能卡住另一块形状互补的珠子团
scene: 营养师说每餐都要有足够的蛋白质。 A protein folds into a shape that lets it bind one substrate and one partner, and nothing else.
sceneCN: 这里 protein 指「蛋白质分子」（第 1 个义项：由氨基酸链折叠成的生物大分子）；形状决定了它能结合谁。图中可辨识物件：珠链、折叠成的团块、表面凹槽、互补的结合面；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 蛋白质（可数，复数 proteins；指该物质整体时也可不可数）

senses.title: A chain folded into a working shape
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质：折叠成形的氨基酸链
senses.definition: a macromolecule made of one or more chains of amino acids folded into a defined three-dimensional shape
senses.definitionCN: 由一条或多条氨基酸链折叠成确定三维形状的生物大分子
senses.example: Haemoglobin is a protein built from four folded chains.
senses.exampleCN: 血红蛋白是由四条折叠链构成的蛋白质。
senses.why: Greek prōteios meant 'primary', and the name was given because such substances were thought to be the primary stuff of nutrition; the modern molecule sense grew from that label.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 prōteios 意为「首要的」，命名时认为这类物质是营养的首要成分；现代「分子」义正是在这个标签上发展出来的。

senses.title: Sequence and fold
senses.definition: the internal plan of a protein: the order of amino acids and the way that order folds
senses.definitionCN: 蛋白质的内部方案：氨基酸的排列顺序，以及这一顺序折叠的方式
senses.example: A single wrong amino acid can spoil the fold of the whole protein.
senses.exampleCN: 一个氨基酸出错就可能毁掉整个蛋白质的折叠。
senses.why: once the chain was sequenced, the word covered not only the substance but the architecture that makes it work.
senses.whyCN: 当链被测序后，这个词不仅指物质，也指让它工作的构造。

senses.title: The nutrient on a plate
senses.titleCN: 营养义：膳食中的蛋白质
senses.definition: the component of food that supplies amino acids, spoken of in amounts and quality
senses.definitionCN: 食物中提供氨基酸的成分，常按数量与质量来谈
senses.example: Beans and rice together supply a complete set of protein.
senses.exampleCN: 豆类与米饭搭配可提供完整的蛋白质。
senses.why: because the molecule is what the body rebuilds from food, the same word names the nutrient class on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体正是用食物重建这种分子，同一个词也指盘中的那类营养素。

senses.title: A job description, not a shape
senses.titleCN: 功能类别：按工作分工的蛋白质
senses.definition: a class of molecules grouped by what they do, such as enzymes, structural proteins, transporters and signals
senses.definitionCN: 按功能归类的分子，如酶、结构蛋白、运输蛋白与信号蛋白
senses.example: Collagen is a structural protein; insulin is a signal protein.
senses.exampleCN: 胶原蛋白是结构蛋白；胰岛素是信号蛋白。
senses.why: since shape serves a task, the word is also used to sort proteins by the task rather than by the fold.
senses.whyCN: 由于形状服务于任务，这个词也被用来按任务而非按折叠方式给蛋白质分类。

senses.title: Measured in a lab
senses.titleCN: 表达与水平：实验中的蛋白量
senses.definition: the amount of a particular protein made by a cell or sample, as measured in experiments
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或样本中某种特定蛋白质的生成量，以实验方式测定
senses.example: The tumour showed high protein expression of the receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤中受体的蛋白表达量很高。
senses.why: laboratory practice turns the substance into a quantity, so 'protein' can mean a measured level rather than a molecule.
senses.whyCN: 实验室实践把这种物质变成一种量，因此 protein 可以指被测定的水平，而非分子本身。

senses.title: Separated and detected
senses.titleCN: 纯化与检测：实验台上的蛋白操作
senses.definition: the substance as an object of purification, blotting and detection
senses.definitionCN: 作为纯化、印迹与检测对象的该物质
senses.example: The protein was purified from bacterial cultures and run on a gel.
senses.exampleCN: 该蛋白从细菌培养物中纯化，并在凝胶上电泳。
senses.why: methods name their object by the material, so a gel band or a blot is simply called protein.
senses.whyCN: 方法学以其材料来命名对象，因此凝胶条带或印迹就被直接称为 protein。

senses.title: The whole set at once
senses.definition: the entire complement of proteins in a cell or tissue, studied as a set
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或组织中全部蛋白质的总体，作为一个集合来研究
senses.example: Proteomic analysis compares thousands of proteins between healthy and sick tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质组分析比较健康与患病组织间数千种蛋白质。
senses.why: high-throughput methods made the collective countable, so the singular word can also stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 高通量方法使这个集合变得可计数，因此单数形式也可指整个集合。

senses.title: Designed and rebuilt
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质工程：改造与设计
senses.definition: a molecule treated as something that can be redesigned, fused or synthesized
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可以重新设计、融合或合成的分子的蛋白质
senses.example: Engineers added a tag to the protein so it could be captured.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给该蛋白加了一个标签，以便把它捕获。
senses.why: when folding is understood as a code, the substance becomes a design space, and the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 当折叠被理解为一种编码，这种物质就成了设计空间，这个词也随之进入该用法。

intro.en: Protein was coined in 1838 from Greek prōteios 'primary', a word built on prōtos 'first'. It reached English through French protéine.
intro.cn: protein 于 1838 年由希腊 prōteios「首要的」造出，该词基于 prōtos「第一」。它经法语 protéine 进入英语。

items.en: prōtos meant 'first, foremost', and prōteios 'primary, of the first rank'. The compound behind them is a Greek formation, not a Latin one.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前」，prōteios 意为「首要的、第一等的」。其背后的构词属希腊语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Jöns Jacob Berzelius proposed the name protéine for the substance Mulder described as a primary constituent of living matter. The date is well recorded; the exact wording of the proposal is not.
items.cn: Jöns Jacob Berzelius 为 Mulder 所述「生命物质的首要成分」提议了 protéine 这一名称。年份有明确记录，提议的原话则无存。

items.en: Generally thought: the name reflects the belief that this substance was the primary material of nutrition and of the body; the reasoning is reported second-hand and not fully documented.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个名字反映了当时认为该物质是营养与身体的首要材料；其推理为二手记载，并未完整留存。

items.en: English protein appears in the nineteenth century through French; the earliest citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 protein 于 19 世纪经法语传入；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry established the amino acid chain and the folded structure, widening the word from a substance to an architecture.
items.cn: 20 世纪的化学确立了氨基酸链与折叠结构，把该词从一种物质扩展到一种构造。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of prōtos before Greek is unsettled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction; the earliest English date for protein is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：prōtos 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，凡给出的印欧形式均属重构；protein 的最早英语书证亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words that name related molecules or roles.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同族的形近词；第二组是命名相关分子或角色的词。

entries.tag: not from pr tos at all
entries.definition: Means 'ever-changing, versatile', from Proteus, the shape-shifting sea god. It shares letters with protein but comes from a different Greek name.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「多变、多才多艺」，来自会变形的海神 Proteus；与 protein 只是拼写相近，来源是另一个希腊专名。

entries.definition: A protein-digesting enzyme. It is named with -ase 'enzyme', so it is a tool that acts on proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分解蛋白质的酶；由 -ase「酶」构成，是作用于蛋白质的工具。

entries.definition: All the proteins of a cell or tissue, named with -ome 'complete set'. It is a collection, not one molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个细胞或组织的全部蛋白质，由 -ome「全集」构成；是集合，不是单个分子。

entries.definition: A short amino acid chain, from Greek peptos 'digested', not from prōtos. Peptides are shorter than proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指短氨基酸链，来自希腊 peptos「被消化的」，并非 prōtos；肽比蛋白质短。

entries.definition: A long chain of amino acids before folding is considered; a protein is the folded, working object.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚未考虑折叠的长氨基酸链；protein 指折叠后能工作的对象。

entries.definition: A catalyst made of protein or RNA. Many enzymes are proteins, but not all proteins are enzymes.
entries.definitionCN: 由蛋白质或 RNA 构成的催化剂；许多酶是蛋白质，但并非所有蛋白质都是酶。

entries.definition: The single building block; a protein is a chain of them.
entries.definitionCN: 单个构建单元；蛋白质是由它们连成的链。

entries.definition: Any substance that nourishes. Protein is one nutrient among several, alongside fat and carbohydrate.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何提供营养的物质；蛋白质是与脂肪、碳水化合物并列的一种营养素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prōteios 'primary': the substance once thought to be the first stuff of the body.
normal.cn: prōteios「首要的」：这曾被当作身体的第一种材料。

normal.en: The family runs protein, proteome, proteomics, proteinase, proteolysis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protein、proteome、proteomics、proteinase、proteolysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: protein structure, protein folding, protein expression, protein purification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：蛋白质结构、折叠、表达、纯化。

normal.en: A protein is a chain that folds; a peptide is a short chain; an enzyme is one kind of protein.
normal.cn: 蛋白质是折叠的链；肽是短链；酶是蛋白质的一种。

normal.en: Structure decides function: the fold makes the pocket, and the pocket decides the partner.
normal.cn: 结构决定功能：折叠造出凹槽，凹槽决定结合对象。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace of coloured beads crushed into a ball with dents and ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一条彩色珠链被揉成一团，表面有凹坑与凸棱。

abstract.en: Picture a key that is also made of beads, so its shape can be rewritten bead by bead.
abstract.cn: 想象一把也由珠子构成的钥匙，其形状可以逐颗改写。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where the same ingredient is used as fuel, as brick and as signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，同一种材料既当燃料，又当砖块，还当信号。

examples.en: Heating denatures the protein, so the egg white turns solid.
examples.cn: 加热使蛋白质变性，因此蛋白凝固。

examples.en: Athletes often eat more protein than they strictly need.
examples.cn: 运动员常摄入超过实际所需的蛋白质。

examples.en: The protein was tagged with a fluorescent label for imaging.
examples.cn: 该蛋白被加上荧光标签以便成像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）上去的（tein）一团」——氨基酸连成链再揉成一团，构成身体的首要材料 → 蛋白质

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」→ prōteios「首要的」→ 法语 protéine（1838，Berzelius 提议）→ 英语 protein。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a chain folds into a shape, and that shape is then read as an architecture, a nutrient, a job class, a measured level, a laboratory object, a whole set, and finally a design space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一条链折叠成一个形状，而这个形状依次被读成构造、营养素、岗位类别、测定值、实验对象、全集，最后是设计空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bead chain crumpled into a lump whose dents fit one partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条珠链被揉成团块，其凹处只与一个对象相合。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: the folded chain is the basic referent of the word.
branches.cn: 分子本身：折叠的链是该词的基本所指。

branches.en: ARCHITECTURE: sequence plus fold, the plan behind the shape.
branches.cn: 构造：序列加折叠，即形状背后的方案。

branches.en: NUTRIENT: the same substance read as food on a plate.
branches.cn: 营养素：同一种物质被读成盘中的食物。

branches.en: JOB CLASS: proteins sorted by task rather than by fold.
branches.cn: 岗位类别：按任务而非按折叠方式分类的蛋白质。

branches.en: QUANTITY AND DESIGN: measured levels, bench objects, whole sets, and molecules rewritten by engineers.
branches.cn: 数量与设计：测定水平、实验台对象、全集，以及被工程师改写的分子。

intro.en: Protein is a Greek-derived noun carrying a Greek suffix -eios; English adds the usual Latin-based endings for its family.
intro.cn: protein 是带希腊后缀 -eios 的希腊派生名词；英语为其词族加上通常的拉丁式词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no classical Latin source. New Latin proteinum is a Latinized spelling, while -ase, -ome and proteo- are modern scientific combining forms.
latinIntro.cn: 没有古典拉丁来源。新拉丁语 proteinum 是拉丁化拼写，而 -ase、-ome 与 proteo- 是现代科学组合形式。

items.meaning: the primary substance of nutrition; a folded amino acid chain
items.meaningCN: 营养的首要物质；折叠的氨基酸链
items.example: The protein binds calcium at its centre.
Membrane proteins transport ions across the bilayer.
items.exampleCN: 膜蛋白把离子运过脂双层。

items.meaningCN: 由蛋白质构成的；蛋白状的
items.example: A proteinaceous coat surrounds the spore.
items.exampleCN: 一层蛋白性质的外壳包裹着孢子。

items.example: A serine proteinase digests the collagen.
items.exampleCN: 一种丝氨酸蛋白酶消化胶原。
蛋白质水解会释放出活性激素。

items.meaning: all proteins of a cell or tissue
items.meaningCN: 细胞或组织的全部蛋白质
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组会随压力改变。

items.meaningCN: 大规模研究蛋白质的学科
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质组学需要灵敏的质谱仪。

items.example: Only proteogenic amino acids enter the chain.
items.exampleCN: 只有生蛋白氨基酸能进入链中。

definition_zh: 维生素；維他命
definition_en: one of a group of natural substances needed in very small amounts for health and growth
core_image: 早餐桌上一个小苹果和一个橙色药瓶
scene: 医生翻着化验单，说骨头长得慢不是因为吃得少，而是缺了那样一小片东西。 The doctor said he needed more vitamin D from sunlight and fish.
sceneCN: 这里 vitamin 是「维生素」（第 1 个义项：少量即维持健康与生长的天然物质）；句意为医生说他需要从阳光和鱼里获取更多维生素 D。小苹果与橙色药瓶并放的早餐桌就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 同效维生素；维生素变体

senses.title: A substance the body must get in tiny amounts
senses.definition: one of a set of substances found in food, needed in small amounts, without which growth and health fail
senses.definitionCN: 食物中一组物质的任何一种，只需微量，缺了便生长受损、健康受损
senses.example: The doctor said he needed more vitamin D from sunlight and fish.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他需要从阳光和鱼类中获取更多维生素 D。
senses.why: The word was built to name what the body must find in food, and this is that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就是为指称身体必须从食物中取得的物质而造，这就是它最朴素的一层。

senses.title: A pill or tablet containing it
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a pill or tablet taken as a supplement
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指作为补充剂服用的药片
senses.example: She keeps a bottle of vitamins beside the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 她在水壶边放了一瓶维生素片。
senses.why: The substance is sold in bottles, so the plural came to mean the tablets themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质以瓶装出售，于是复数形式就转而指药片本身。

senses.title: The letter names of the group
senses.definition: the letter and number system, from vitamin A to vitamin K, used to tell the members apart
senses.definitionCN: 用字母与数字区分成员的体系，从维生素 A 到维生素 K
senses.example: Vitamin C is easily lost when vegetables are over-boiled.
senses.exampleCN: 蔬菜煮过头时维生素 C 很容易流失。
senses.why: One family needed separate labels, and chemists simply lettered the members.
senses.whyCN: 同一个家族需要各自的名字，化学家就干脆给成员编上字母。

senses.title: A figuratively nourishing element
senses.definition: a quality or thing that a group needs for health, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体健康所需的东西，用于比喻
senses.example: For a young band, applause is like a vitamin.
senses.exampleCN: 对一支年轻乐队来说，掌声就像维生素。
senses.why: Anything that keeps a thing growing in small doses can be called a vitamin in speech.
senses.whyCN: 凡是少量就能让事物生长起来的东西，在口语里都能被叫作维生素。

intro.en: Vitamin was coined in 1912 by the biochemist Casimir Funk from vita, life, and amine, a nitrogen compound.
intro.cn: vitamin 由生物化学家冯克在 1912 年用 vita（生命）与 amine（胺）拼造而成。

items.en: Vita meant life, and the chemist took it as the first half of his new word.
items.cn: vita 意为生命，化学家取它作新词的前半部分。

items.en: Scientists first believed these substances belonged to a group called amines and joined the two ideas into vitamine.
items.cn: 科学家起初以为这些物质属于胺类，便把两个概念拼成了 vitamine。

items.en: When most proved not to be amines, the e was dropped, but the old spelling had already spread in packets and papers.
items.cn: 后来发现它们大多不是胺，词尾的 e 被删去，但旧拼法已在包装和报刊上流传。

items.en: The letters A to K were assigned to separate the members, and the names hardened around the diet.
items.cn: 人们用 A 到 K 的字母区分各个成员，这些名字便围绕饮食固定下来。

items.en: Twentieth-century advertising, from orange juice to children’s cereals, carried vitamin into ordinary homes.
items.cn: 二十世纪的广告从橙汁到儿童麦片，把 vitamin 带进寻常人家。

note.en: The first group gathers the coinage and its descendants, the second the words about food and what the body needs.
note.cn: 第一组收造词本身及其衍生物，第二组收与食物和身体所需有关的词。

entries.definition: The usual plural, seen on almost every carton.
entries.definitionCN: 常见复数形式

entries.definition: The adjective, related to or full of vitamins.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，与维生素有关或富含维生素

entries.definition: A substance the body turns into a vitamin.
entries.definitionCN: 维生素原

entries.definition: Food with vitamins added after processing.
entries.definitionCN: 加工后添加维生素的食品

entries.definition: Any nourishing substance, of which vitamins are one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 营养素

entries.definition: A simple element such as iron that the body also needs.
entries.definitionCN: 矿物质

entries.definition: A product taken to add what food lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 补充剂

entries.definition: The lack of such a substance, which vitamin cures.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏，维生素所治的正是这种缺失

normalIntro.en: Vitamin is a coined word, so it is remembered by its two halves and by the letters that tag the group.
normalIntro.cn: vitamin 是一个新造词，可以靠它的两个半截，以及给它们编字母的办法来记。

normal.en: Vita is life, so vitamins are the small things life needs.
normal.cn: vita 是生命，维生素就是生命需要的那点小东西。

normal.en: The old spelling vitamine kept an e from amine; the e was later dropped.
normal.cn: 旧拼法 vitamine 保留 amine 里的 e，后来删去。

normal.en: Vitamin C protects the gums; vitamin D comes from the sun.
normal.cn: 维生素 C 护牙龈，维生素 D 来自阳光。

normal.en: A deficiency means the body wanted a vitamin and did not get it.
normal.cn: deficiency 就是身体想要某种维生素却没得到。

normal.en: The bare plural vitamins often means the bottle of pills.
normal.cn: 单说 vitamins 常指那瓶药片。

abstract.en: See thin orange slices and a tiny white tablet side by side.
abstract.cn: 想薄薄的橙子片与一粒白色小药片并排。

abstract.en: Feel the sun on your arms, working unseen as a vitamin.
abstract.cn: 感受阳光落在手臂上，无声地像维生素一样起作用。

abstract.en: Picture a body with one missing piece, small as a grain.
abstract.cn: 想一具身体只缺一粒米那样大的一块。

examples.en: Oranges are a good source of vitamin C.
examples.cn: 橙子是维生素 C 的良好来源。

examples.en: Too little vitamin D weakens the bones.
examples.cn: 维生素 D 过少会使骨头变脆。

examples.en: The label lists every vitamin added to the cereal.
examples.cn: 标签列出了加进麦片的每一种维生素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维他命」——这是旧时音译，维他之命，小小一粒，替他续命。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）+ amine（胺）→ 1912 年造词 vitamine → 1920 年代改拼 vitamin。

sensesIntro.en: A coined scientific word became a household one: a substance needed in trace amounts, the bottle of pills, the letter system, and any nourishment an effort needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个造出来的科学词变成了家常词：只需微量的物质、那瓶药片、字母编号体系，以及任何努力所需的养料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny tablet beside an orange.
core.cn: 核心意象：橙子旁的一小粒药片。

branches.en: The substance branch: something from sunlight and fish.
branches.cn: 物质分支：来自阳光与鱼的东西。

branches.en: The bottle branch: pills kept beside the kettle.
branches.cn: 药瓶分支：水壶边的药片。

branches.en: The naming branch: lost when greens boil too long.
branches.cn: 命名分支：青菜煮太久就会流失。

branches.en: The figurative branch: applause for a young band.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：年轻乐队得到的掌声。

branches.en: The diet branch: the letter on the cereal label.
branches.cn: 饮食分支：麦片标签上的字母。

intro.en: Vitamin joins the Latin life root vit- to the chemical word amine, so it is a hyphenated piece of history.
intro.cn: vitamin 把拉丁生命词根 vit- 与化学词 amine 拼合，是带着删改痕迹的历史合成词。

latinIntro.en: The first half, vit- and vita, is recorded Latin for life; the second half, amine, comes from ammonia.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 vit-、vita 是有文献的拉丁语「生命」，后半 amine 来自 ammonia（氨）。

items.example: The Latin half of the coinage.
The chemist merged it with the life root.
items.exampleCN: 化学家把它与生命词根合并。

items.example: The word lost its e when the theory changed.
items.exampleCN: 理论改变后这个词失去了 e。

items.example: It names the stuff rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 它命名物质而不是动作。

definition_zh: 流行病；（坏事）迅速蔓延；流行性的
definition_en: a disease that spreads quickly through many people, or the rapid spread of something bad
core_image: 一条街接一条街，病人越来越多，像波纹扩散
scene: 那年冬天，流感在城里迅速蔓延。 That winter, a flu epidemic swept through the city.
sceneCN: 这里 epidemic 是「流行病」（第 1 个义项：在人群中快速传播的疾病）；句意：那年冬天，流感在城里迅速蔓延。

senses.title: A quickly spreading disease
senses.definition: an infectious disease that spreads rapidly among many people in an area
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地区人群中迅速传播的传染病
senses.example: The city closed its schools during the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情期间，这座城市关闭了学校。
senses.why: The Greek root means among the people, so a disease running through a whole population is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「在民众之中」，因此贯穿整个人群的疾病是第一个义项。

senses.title: The rapid spread of something bad
senses.definition: a rapid increase or spread of something harmful or unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 有害或不受欢迎之物的迅速增加或扩散
senses.example: Experts warn of an epidemic of online fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 专家警告网络诈骗正在迅速蔓延。
senses.why: The image of disease spreading is borrowed for any harmful trend.
senses.whyCN: 疾病传播的意象被借用来指任何有害趋势。

senses.title: Affecting many people at once
senses.definition: used as an adjective for something that spreads widely at one time
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指在某一时期广泛传播的事物
senses.example: Obesity has become an epidemic problem in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 肥胖在许多国家已成为普遍性问题。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the same spreading idea and applies it to conditions or problems.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留同样的「扩散」概念，并用于状况或问题。

intro.en: Epidemic comes from Greek epidemos, among the people, from epi-, upon, and demos, the people.
intro.cn: epidemic 来自希腊语 epidemos（在民众之中），由 epi-（在上）与 demos（民众）构成。

items.en: Demos means the people.
items.cn: demos 意为民众。

items.en: Epi- means upon or among.
items.cn: epi- 意为在上或在……之中。

items.en: Epidemos means among the people.
items.cn: epidemos 意为在民众之中。

items.en: Epidemia names a disease visiting a whole population.
items.cn: epidemia 指降临整个人群的疾病。

items.en: French épidémie carries the medical sense.
items.cn: 法语 épidémie 保留医学含义。

items.en: Modern English extends epidemic to any rapid spread.
items.cn: 现代英语把 epidemic 扩展到任何迅速蔓延。

note.en: Epidemic is a spreading word from the demos family, near outbreak words and near its own technical relatives.
note.cn: epidemic 是来自 demos 词族的「扩散」词，与疫情词以及自身技术词族相邻。

entries.definition: the study of how diseases spread
entries.definitionCN: 流行病学

entries.definition: a specialist in disease spread
entries.definitionCN: 流行病学家

entries.definition: regularly found in a particular place
entries.definitionCN: 地方性的

entries.definition: a sudden start of disease or violence
entries.definitionCN: 暴发；突然发生

entries.definition: a deadly widespread disease
entries.definitionCN: 瘟疫

entries.definition: a disease spreading across the world
entries.definitionCN: 全球性流行病

normalIntro.en: Epidemic is epi- plus demos: a disease that settles upon the whole people.
normalIntro.cn: epidemic 是 epi- 加 demos：一种落到全体民众身上的疾病。

normal.en: Demos means people, and epidemic spreads among people.
normal.cn: demos 意为民众，epidemic 就在人群中传播。

normal.en: A flu epidemic sends many people to bed at once.
normal.cn: 流感流行会让许多人同时病倒。

normal.en: Epidemic proportions means a very large scale.
normal.cn: epidemic proportions 表示极大的规模。

normal.en: Epidemiology is the study of how epidemics move.
normal.cn: epidemiology 研究流行病如何传播。

normal.en: Compare endemic: endemic stays in one place, epidemic spreads.
normal.cn: 对比 endemic：endemic 局限一地，epidemic 会扩散。

abstract.en: Picture rings of illness widening street by street.
abstract.cn: 想象疾病像波纹一样一条街一条街地扩大。

abstract.en: Imagine a red dot spreading across a map of a city.
abstract.cn: 想象一个红点在城市地图上扩散。

abstract.en: Think of a rumor passing from door to door.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言从一扇门传到另一扇门。

examples.en: Doctors worked day and night to stop the epidemic.
examples.cn: 医生们日夜工作以阻止流行病蔓延。

examples.en: The report describes an epidemic of loneliness among the elderly.
examples.cn: 报告描述了老年人中普遍存在的孤独问题。

examples.en: Epidemic diseases spread fastest where people live close together.
examples.cn: 在人们居住密集的地方，流行性疾病传播得最快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「epi + demic」——疾病「压在」众人头上，就成了流行病；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ demos（民众）→ epidemos（在民众之中）→ epidemia（流行病）→ 英语 epidemic，核心义「在人群之中扩散」。

sensesIntro.en: Epidemic begins as a disease among the people, extends to any harmful spread, and then works as an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: epidemic 从人群中的疾病开始，扩展到任何有害的蔓延，再作形容词使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: illness moving through a whole population.
core.cn: 核心意象：疾病穿过整个人群。

branches.en: A spreading disease is the original medical sense.
branches.cn: 传播中的疾病是最初的医学义项。

branches.en: Any harmful spread borrows the disease image.
branches.cn: 任何有害蔓延都借用了疾病的意象。

branches.en: The adjective describes what affects many at once.
branches.cn: 形容词描述同时影响许多人的事物。

branches.en: Both a virus and a fraud wave move quickly through crowds.
branches.cn: 病毒与诈骗浪潮都在人群中快速移动。

branches.en: A disease becomes epidemic when it reaches many people.
branches.cn: 疾病在波及许多人时成为流行性的。

intro.en: Epidemic is built from Greek epi- and demos, with a large English family in epidemiology and its forms.
intro.cn: epidemic 由希腊语 epi- 与 demos 构成，英语词族在 epidemiology 及其派生词中扩展。

latinIntro.en: Greek epi- means upon, and demos means the people.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 epi- 意为在上，demos 意为民众。

items.example: Epi- places the disease upon the people.
items.exampleCN: epi- 把疾病置于民众之上。
epidemos 把两部分组合起来。

items.example: Epidemia is the Greek medical noun.
items.exampleCN: epidemia 是希腊语医学名词。
epidemiology 研究疾病如何传播。

definition_zh: adj. 传染的，接触传染的；有感染力的
definition_en: spreading by contact, or spreading easily to others
core_image: 一个咳嗽让整间屋子的人都缩了缩肩
scene: 麻疹传染性极强，必须隔离。 Measles is highly contagious and must be isolated.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contagious 指传染的；句意是麻疹传染性极强。

senses.title: Spreading by contact
senses.definition: passing from one person to another by contact
senses.definitionCN: 通过接触从一人传给另一人
senses.example: Measles is highly contagious.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹传染性极强。
senses.why: Latin contingere means to touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 contingere 意为接触。

senses.title: Spreading by feeling
senses.definition: spreading quickly as a mood or manner
senses.definitionCN: 以情绪或神态迅速传开
senses.example: Her laughter is contagious.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声很有感染力。
senses.why: The touch becomes a touch of mood.
senses.whyCN: 身体的接触变成情绪的感染。

intro.en: Contagious comes from Latin contingere, to touch.
intro.cn: contagious 源自拉丁语 contingere，意为接触。

items.en: Tangere means to touch.
items.cn: tangere 意为接触。

items.en: Contingere means to touch together.
items.cn: contingere 意为接触到。

items.en: Contagio names the touch of disease.
items.cn: contagio 指疾病的接触传播。

items.en: English used it of plague.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语用它指瘟疫。

items.en: It spread to moods and laughter.
items.cn: 十九世纪扩展到情绪与笑声。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the contagi- stem; the near-meaning group names spreading illness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 contagi- 词干；近义组列出传播的疾病。

entries.definition: The spreading of disease.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病的传播。

entries.definition: Sharing a border.
entries.definitionCN: 接壤的。

entries.definition: In a spreading way.
entries.definitionCN: 以传染的方式。

entries.definition: Spreading by germs.
entries.definitionCN: 由病菌传播的。

entries.definition: Likely to pass to others.
entries.definitionCN: 容易传给他人的。

entries.definition: Able to spread between people.
entries.definitionCN: 可在人与人之间传播的。

entries.definition: Reaching more people.
entries.definitionCN: 波及更多人的。

normalIntro.en: Contagious things pass by touch, whether germs or giggles.
normalIntro.cn: contagious 之物靠接触传递，无论是病菌还是笑声。

normal.en: Tangere means to touch.
normal.cn: tangere 意为接触。

normal.en: Contingere means to touch upon.
normal.cn: contingere 意为接触到。

normal.en: A contagious disease touches others.
normal.cn: 传染病会触及他人。

normal.en: A contagious laugh touches moods.
normal.cn: 有感染力的笑触及情绪。

normal.en: The noun is contagion.
normal.cn: 名词是 contagion。

abstract.en: A cough crossing a room.
abstract.cn: 穿过房间的一声咳嗽。

abstract.en: A giggle passing down a row.
abstract.cn: 沿着一排传开的轻笑。

abstract.en: A cheer spreading through a stand.
abstract.cn: 在看台上蔓延的欢呼。

examples.en: The illness is contagious before symptoms show.
examples.cn: 这种病在症状出现前就会传染。

examples.en: Her good mood was contagious.
examples.cn: 她的好心情很有感染力。

examples.en: Keep contagious patients apart.
examples.cn: 把传染病人隔开。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（共同）+ tag（接触）+ -ious（…的）→ 一接触就传开，即传染的。

root: 拉丁 con（共同）+ tangere（接触）→ contagio（传染）→ 英语 contagious

sensesIntro.en: Passing from body to body, or from face to face.
sensesIntro.cn: 在身体之间，或在表情之间传开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cough making a whole room flinch
core.cn: 核心意象：一声咳嗽让全屋人一缩

branches.en: A disease that crosses a table.
branches.cn: 越过餐桌的疾病。

branches.en: A ward kept apart.
branches.cn: 被隔开的病房。

branches.en: A laugh that runs down a row.
branches.cn: 沿排传开的笑声。

branches.en: A cheer that lifts a stand.
branches.cn: 让看台振奋的欢呼。

branches.en: One touch, a wider circle.
branches.cn: 一次接触，更大的圈。

intro.en: Contagious carries the Latin touch root tangere.
intro.cn: contagious 带着拉丁语表「接触」的词根 tangere。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere is to touch and contagio is a touching of disease.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 意为接触，contagio 指疾病的接触传播。

definition_zh: adj. 慢性的；（问题）长期的；积习难改的
definition_en: lasting a long time and hard to cure; happening again and again over a long period
core_image: 病历上连续几年的同一行诊断
scene: 他有多年的腰痛，属于慢性问题。 He has had back pain for years, a chronic problem.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chronic 指慢性的；句意是他多年的腰痛属于慢性问题。

senses.title: Long-lasting illness
senses.definition: of an illness that lasts a long time and is hard to cure
senses.definitionCN: 指病程长、难以治愈的疾病
senses.example: She has chronic asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 她患有慢性哮喘。
senses.why: Greek khronikos means of time, from khronos, time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 khronikos 意为与时间有关的，源自 khronos（时间）。

senses.title: A long-running problem
senses.definition: continuing for a long time and difficult to solve
senses.definitionCN: 持续很久且难以解决的
senses.example: The city has a chronic housing shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市长期住房短缺。
senses.why: The medical sense widened to any long habit or problem.
senses.whyCN: 医学义扩大到任何长期习惯或问题。

definition_en: gentle and kindly, or not harmful, especially of a tumour or climate
core_image: 一株安静无害的小圆影，像晒着太阳的云
scene: 体检报告摊开在桌上，医生微笑着指向那行字。 The doctor smiled and said the tumour was benign.

senses.title: Gentle and kindly in manner

senses.example: The professor gave the nervous student a benign smile.
senses.exampleCN: 教授朝紧张的学生投去和蔼的一笑。
senses.why: Bene means well and gen- relates to birth or nature, so the nature itself is good.

senses.title: Not harmful, especially of a tumour
senses.definition: not dangerous to health, especially not spreading or cancerous
senses.definitionCN: 不危及健康，尤指不扩散、非癌性的
senses.example: The doctor smiled and said the tumour was benign.
senses.exampleCN: 医生笑着说肿瘤是良性的。
senses.why: A good-natured growth stays mild and does no harm.

senses.title: Mild and favourable, as of climate or conditions
senses.definition: pleasantly mild, as weather or an environment that favours growth
senses.definitionCN: 气候、环境温和，宜于生长

senses.exampleCN: 这座小岛全年气候温和宜人。
senses.why: Goodness spreads to surroundings that nurture life.
senses.whyCN: 「良善」扩展到滋养生命的周遭环境。

intro.cn: benign 来自拉丁语 benignus，由 bene「好」与 genus、gignere「出生、生育」构成。

items.en: the root gene- meant to give birth, to beget.
items.cn: 词根 gene- 意为「生育、产生」（重构形式）。

items.en: benignus meant kind, good by nature.
items.cn: 拉丁语 benignus 意为「天性良善的、仁慈的」。

items.en: benigne carried the word into French.
items.cn: 古法语 benigne 使该词传入法语。

items.en: English borrowed benign in the fourteenth century for kind rulers and mild weather.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 benign，形容仁君与温和天气。

items.en: medical use for harmless tumours became its best-known sense.
items.cn: 「良性肿瘤」的医学用法成为如今最广为人知的义项。

definition_zh: （使）断裂；裂缝；骨折；岩体破裂；分裂
definition_en: to break or crack a hard solid, or the break itself, especially in bone or rock
core_image: 一块完好的石板被凿子沿着一条细线敲开，断面新鲜而锋利
scene: 地质实验室里，学生把岩芯夹在台钳上，准备沿薄弱面敲开。 A geologist uses a chisel to fracture the core sample and expose a fresh surface.
sceneCN: 这里 fracture 是动词「使断裂、敲裂」（第 1 个义项：把坚硬固体沿薄弱面破开）；句意为地质学家用凿子敲裂岩芯样品，露出新鲜断面。

裂缝；断裂；骨折；岩体破裂

derivatives.zh: 断裂的；分裂的；支离破碎的

碎片；片段（同出 frangere 的另一支）

使折射（re- 加 frangere，指光线折断）

senses.title: Break a hard solid on purpose
senses.definition: to break or crack a hard material such as rock, metal or glass
senses.definitionCN: 使岩石、金属、玻璃等坚硬材料破裂或出现裂缝
senses.example: A geologist uses a chisel to fracture the core sample.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家用凿子敲裂岩芯样品。
senses.why: fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from frangere, to break; the verb is the act that produces a fractura.
senses.whyCN: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，源自动词 frangere「打破」；动词义就是产生一道断裂的动作。

senses.title: The crack that results
senses.definition: a crack or line of breakage in a solid object
senses.definitionCN: 固体物件上出现的裂缝或断线
senses.example: A hairline fracture ran across the marble slab.
senses.exampleCN: 一条发丝般的细裂缝横过大理石板。
senses.why: Latin fractura named both the act and its result, and English kept the same double life in one noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fractura 同时指动作与结果，英语把这个双重身份原样保留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Break a bone
senses.definition: to crack or break a bone in the body
senses.definitionCN: 使身体中的骨头裂开或折断
senses.example: He fractured his wrist when he fell off the ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，手腕骨折了。
senses.why: a bone is the hardest solid in the body, so the general sense of breaking a hard thing settled naturally on bone.
senses.whyCN: 骨头是身体里最硬的固体，因此「敲断硬物」的一般义自然落在骨折上。

senses.title: A break in the rock mass
senses.definition: a planar break through rock along which the two sides have moved or can move
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿岩层、两侧已发生或可能发生位移的破裂面
senses.example: The fault is a fracture that has slipped many times.
senses.exampleCN: 这条断层是一条多次滑动的破裂面。
senses.why: geology took the everyday noun and made it precise: a fracture is any break, a fault is one that has actually slipped.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把日常名词精确化：fracture 泛指破裂，fault 专指真正发生过滑动的那一条。

senses.title: Split a group into camps
senses.titleCN: 使团体分裂成对立阵营
senses.definition: to divide a group, party or alliance into opposing parts
senses.definitionCN: 使团体、政党或联盟分裂为对立的几部分
senses.example: The dispute fractured the alliance into three camps.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端把联盟分裂成三个阵营。
senses.why: the image of a solid breaking into pieces was transferred from stone to social bodies, which also lose their wholeness.
senses.whyCN: 固体碎成数块的意象被移用到社会群体上，因为群体同样会失去完整。

senses.title: A split in unity or agreement
senses.definition: a division or breach in something previously united, such as trust or consensus
senses.definitionCN: 原本统一之物（如信任或共识）出现的分裂或缺口
senses.example: The report exposed a fracture in the coalition's common position.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告暴露出联盟共同立场上的一道裂口。
senses.why: the noun sense extends the physical crack to anything that can no longer be described as one piece.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把物理裂缝扩展到一切不再能被称作「一整块」的事物。

senses.title: The way a mineral breaks
senses.definition: the characteristic surface shape a mineral shows when it breaks other than along cleavage planes
senses.definitionCN: 矿物不沿解理面断开时所呈现的特征断面形态
senses.example: Quartz shows a conchoidal fracture rather than flat cleavage.
senses.exampleCN: 石英呈现贝壳状断口，而不是平整的解理面。
senses.why: mineralogy needed a word for the surface left by breaking, and fracture already meant exactly that result.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学需要一个词指断裂留下的表面，而 fracture 本来就表示这个结果。

senses.title: Break the continuity of something abstract
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：打断某种连续性
senses.definition: to break the continuity or smooth working of a system, narrative or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 打断系统、叙事或关系的连续性或顺畅运转
senses.example: One missing shipment can fracture a delicate supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 一次缺货就可能打断一条脆弱的供应链。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the core gesture: something that was continuous is now interrupted by a break.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留核心动作：原本连续的东西，如今被一道断口打断。

intro.en: Fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from the verb frangere, to break, whose past participle is fractus. The word entered English in the fifteenth century, first as the medical name for a broken bone.
intro.cn: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，出自动词 frangere「打破」，其过去分词为 fractus。该词于 15 世纪进入英语，最初是骨折的医学名称。

items.en: Frangere meant to break, shatter or smash. Its past participle fractus supplied the stem frac- seen in fracture, fraction and fragment.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破、击碎、砸碎」。其过去分词 fractus 提供了 fracture、fraction、fragment 中所见的 frac- 词干。

items.en: Fractura was the noun of result, a breaking or the breach produced by it, used for broken bones as well as broken objects.
items.cn: fractura 是结果名词，指「断裂」或断裂造成的破口，既用于断骨，也用于破碎的物件。

items.en: English took fracture in the fifteenth century as a term for a broken bone, alongside the older verb break.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借入 fracture，作为骨折的术语，与更古老的动词 break 并存。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to rock masses and to manufactured materials, where a fracture is a plane of breakage.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，该词被用于岩体与人工材料，其中 fracture 指一个破裂面。

items.en: In modern usage a society, party or narrative can be fractured, extending the stone image to anything that loses its wholeness.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，社会、政党或叙事都可以被 fracture，把石头的意象扩展到一切失去完整性的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the link of frangere to a reconstructed Indo-European root for breaking is a standard reconstruction, not a recorded form; the first date of the geological sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：frangere 与重构的印欧语「打破」词根之间的联系属于标准重构，并非有记录的形式；地质义的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin breaking stock; group two holds near neighbours that also describe damage or division.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「打破」词干的词；第二组是同样表示损坏或分裂的近义词。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: cracked, split or disjointed, as in a fractured skull or a fractured story.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的过去分词作形容词：裂开的、分裂的、支离破碎的，如骨折的头骨或破碎的叙事。

entries.definition: From the same frangere stock: a piece broken off something larger, so it names the result rather than the break.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 frangere：从更大物体上掉下的一块，指结果而非断裂本身。

entries.definition: Also from fractus, but it shifted to a numerical part of a whole and no longer means a physical break.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 fractus，但语义转向「整体的数值部分」，不再指物理断裂。

entries.definition: From frangere through French: easily broken, describing a quality rather than an event.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自 frangere：容易破碎的，描述性质而非事件。

entries.definition: A narrow line of breakage or a sharp splitting sound; it can be smaller than a fracture and need not separate the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的裂线或清脆的爆裂声；可以比 fracture 更轻，且两半不必分离。

entries.definition: The general English verb for separating into pieces; fracture is its technical and medical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示分成数块的一般英语动词；fracture 是它技术化、医学化的对应词。

entries.definition: To divide along a line, often cleanly, as wood splits; it stresses separation rather than shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 沿一条线分开，常指干脆地劈开，如木头裂开；强调分离而非碎成多块。

entries.definition: A sudden tearing or bursting of something under pressure, such as a pipe or a tendon; it adds force to the idea of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 受压之物突然撕裂或爆开，如管道或肌腱；在「断裂」之上加了「受力爆裂」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: frac- is the broken stem: frangere broke things, and fractus is the broken result.
normal.cn: frac- 就是「断」的词干：frangere 打破东西，fractus 是打破的结果。

normal.en: The family runs fracture, fractured, fracturing, fraction, fragment, fragile and refract.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fracture、fractured、fracturing、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

normal.en: Medical phrases fix the bone sense: hairline fracture, stress fracture, compound fracture.
normal.cn: 医学搭配固定了骨折义：细微骨折、应力性骨折、开放性骨折。

normal.en: Geology pairs it with fault and fracture zone, where the break is a plane in rock.
normal.cn: 地质学把它与断层、断裂带配对，此时断口是岩体中的一个面。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: fracture a bone, fracture a rock, fracture an alliance.
normal.cn: 动词直接带宾语：使骨折、敲裂岩石、使联盟分裂。

abstract.en: Picture a plate that looks whole until a hairline runs across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只看似完好的盘子，直到一条细线横穿而过。

abstract.en: Picture a team photo with one person cut out of the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张团队合影，其中一个人被从画面里裁掉。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that stops in the middle because the thought itself broke.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说到一半就停住，因为那个念头本身断了。

examples.en: The impact fractured the limestone into angular blocks.
examples.cn: 撞击把石灰岩碎成有棱角的岩块。

examples.en: She fractured her ankle while stepping off the curb.
examples.cn: 她在下路缘时扭断了脚踝。

examples.en: The vote fractured the party along regional lines.
examples.cn: 这次投票使该党沿地域界线分裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fract（断）+ ure」——像石头被敲出一道缝 → 断裂、骨折、分裂

root: 拉丁 frangere「打破」的过去分词 fractus + 名词后缀 -ura → fractura「断裂」；英语 fracture。同族含 fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: a hard thing loses its wholeness. The event is then named as a noun, located in bone, made a plane in rock, and finally applied to groups, agreements, mineral surfaces and systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个事件展开：坚硬之物失去完整。这个事件先被名词化，再落到骨头、岩体中的平面，最后用于群体、共识、矿物断面与系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound slab that acquires a sharp new line and is no longer one piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块完好的石板出现一道锋利的新线，从此不再是一整块。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the verb names the blow, the noun names the line it leaves.
branches.cn: 动作与结果：动词指那一下敲击，名词指它留下的那条线。

branches.en: BONE: the body's hardest solid is the most personal place a fracture can happen.
branches.cn: 骨头：身体里最硬的固体，是断裂最能切身发生的地方。

branches.en: ROCK AND MINERAL: geology turns the break into a measurable plane or surface.
branches.cn: 岩石与矿物：地质学把断裂变成可测量的平面或断面。

branches.en: SOCIAL SPLIT: a group, like a slab, can lose its wholeness along a line.
branches.cn: 社会分裂：群体和石板一样，会沿一条线失去完整。

branches.en: SYSTEM BREAK: continuity itself is what snaps in the abstract use.
branches.cn: 系统中断：抽象用法里断掉的是连续性本身。

intro.en: Fracture is a Latin noun of result built from a verbal stem plus a suffix, and the same stem recurs across English.
intro.cn: fracture 是由动词词干加后缀构成的拉丁结果名词，同一词干在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere, fractus and fractura give fracture, fraction, fragment, fragile, refract and frangible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frangere、fractus 与 fractura 衍生 fracture、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract 与 frangible。

items.example: The stem frac- carries the result of breaking.
items.exampleCN: 词干 frac- 承载「打破之后的结果」。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Fractura is the result noun built on the participle.
items.exampleCN: fractura 是在分词之上构成的结果名词。

items.example: The chisel fracture left a clean edge.
items.exampleCN: 凿出的断裂留下干净的边。

items.meaningCN: 断裂的；分裂的；支离破碎的
items.example: The fractured rock face showed several sets of joints.
items.exampleCN: 断裂的岩面显出好几组节理。

items.meaning: a breaking into parts, hence a numerical part
items.meaningCN: 分成部分，后指数值上的分数
items.example: Only a fraction of the sample survived.
items.exampleCN: 样品中只有一小部分留存。

items.example: Fragments of the core lay on the bench.
items.exampleCN: 岩芯的碎片散在实验台上。

items.example: The fragile shell cracked at a touch.

items.meaning: to bend a ray back as it passes
items.example: Water refracts the light entering it.
items.exampleCN: 水使进入其中的光发生折射。

items.example: The frangible target shattered on impact.

definition_zh: 伤口；创伤；伤害；使受伤；伤害（感情）
definition_en: an injury that breaks the skin or cuts deeply, or to cause such an injury; also to hurt someone's feelings
core_image: 小臂上一道已经结痂的口子，边缘还红着一圈
scene: 包扎完以后，大夫叮嘱这两天别沾水，也别去搬重东西。 The wound on his arm healed quickly, but he still avoided lifting heavy boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 wound 是「伤口」（第 1 个义项：使皮肤破损或深深切开的损伤）；句意为他手臂上的伤口好得很快，但他仍不愿搬重箱子。手臂上那圈还红着的口子，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wound 加 -ed 构成，义为「受伤的」
由 wound 加 -ing 构成，义为「伤人的；刺痛的」
由 wound 加 -less 构成，义为「未受伤的」

senses.title: The physical injury
senses.definition: an injury in which the skin is cut or broken, especially by a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤被切开或打破的损伤，尤指由武器造成
senses.example: The wound on his arm healed quickly, but he still avoided lifting heavy boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 他手臂上的伤口好得很快，但他仍不愿搬重箱子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a blow that breaks the surface of the body, and that body image runs through the others.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是打破身体表面的击伤，这个身体形象贯穿其余义项。

senses.title: To injure
senses.definition: to hurt a person or animal so that the skin or flesh is broken
senses.definitionCN: 使皮肤或皮肉破损地伤害人或动物
senses.example: Two men were wounded in the accident at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 路口那场事故中有两人受伤。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb that names the act which produces it, and the passive is the common shape.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，指造成这个结果的动作，常用被动形式。

senses.title: The hurt that cannot be seen
senses.definition: to damage someone in feeling or reputation, not in the body
senses.definitionCN: 在情感或名誉上而非身体上伤害某人
senses.example: Her remark wounded him more than any accident could have.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句话对他的刺痛，胜过任何一场事故。
senses.why: The body image carries over: an unseen cut in feeling uses the same word as a cut in the skin.
senses.whyCN: 身体形象延续下来：看不见的情感切口，用与皮肤切口同一个词。

senses.title: The injury to a cause
senses.definition: a lasting damage done to a plan, a group or a reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对计划、团体或声誉造成的持久损害
senses.example: The decision was a wound to the trust between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 那个决定是两个镇之间的信任上的一道伤。
senses.why: When the thing hurt is a bond rather than a body, the word still marks while it leaves a lasting mark.
senses.whyCN: 当受伤的不是身体而是联系时，这个词照样留下持久的痕迹。

intro.en: Wound is Old English wund, a physical injury, shared with German Wunde, and unrelated to the past tense of wind.
intro.cn: wound 来自古英语 wund（身体损伤），与德语 Wunde 同源，与 wind 的过去式毫无关系。

items.en: wund meant a cut or a blow that breaks the body.
items.cn: wund 指切开或打破身体的伤。

items.en: The same noun appears in German and Dutch for the same kind of injury.
items.cn: 同一名词在德语与荷兰语里指同样的损伤。

items.en: The word was used for battle injuries and spread to the verb.
items.cn: 这个词用于战伤，并蔓延到动词用法。

items.en: The figurative sense of hurting feelings settled in ordinary use.
items.cn: 伤害感情的比喻义在日常用法中固定下来。

items.en: It is spelled like wound, the past of wind, and the two are pronounced alike but unrelated.
items.cn: 它拼得与 wind 的过去式 wound 一样，两者读音相同却毫无关系。

note.en: The first group holds the forms of this word, including the look-alike past of wind, the second holds other words for injury.
note.cn: 第一组收本词的各种形式，包括形同的 wind 过去式，第二组收其他表示损伤的词。

entries.definition: Hurt, in body or in feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 受伤的

entries.definition: More than one wound, or third person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 伤口（复数）或三单

entries.definition: Twisted or turned, the past of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 缠绕（wind 的过去式）

entries.definition: Physical harm to the body.
entries.definitionCN: 损伤；伤害

entries.definition: The mark left after a wound heals.
entries.definitionCN: 疤痕

entries.definition: An opening made in the skin by something sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 切口；割伤

normalIntro.en: Wound keeps the ou spelling but has a long oo sound, and it must not be confused with the past of wind.
normalIntro.cn: wound 保留了 ou 的拼写，却读长音，且不能与 wind 的过去式混淆。

normal.en: The spelling ou here is regular: wound rhymes with spoon, not with ground.
normal.cn: 这里的 ou 读长音：wound 与 spoon 押韵，不与 ground 押韵。

normal.en: Wound as the past of wind is pronounced differently and means twisted.
normal.cn: 作 wind 的过去式时读音不同，意思是缠绕。

normal.en: Wounded is the usual adjective: a wounded soldier.
normal.cn: 常用形容词是 wounded：a wounded soldier。

normal.en: The verb has three senses: hurt the body, hurt the feelings, hurt a cause.
normal.cn: 这个动词有三义：伤身体、伤感情、伤事业。

normal.en: Lick one's wounds means to rest and recover after a defeat.
normal.cn: lick one's wounds 指受挫后休整恢复。

abstract.en: A line of scab with a red rim still around it.
abstract.cn: 一道结痂的口子，边上一圈还红着。

abstract.en: A bandage still on a forearm two days later.
abstract.cn: 两天后小臂上还缠着绷带。

abstract.en: A sentence that stays with a person far longer than any cut.
abstract.cn: 一句话在人心里留得比任何伤口都久。

examples.en: The wound was small but deep, and it took weeks to close.
examples.cn: 伤口不大却很深，好几周才合上。

examples.en: He was wounded in the shoulder during the match.
examples.cn: 比赛时他肩膀受了伤。

examples.en: Her words had wounded him, even if she meant no harm.
examples.cn: 她的话伤了他，尽管她并无恶意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂」——伤口不能碰，只好捂着。

root: 古英语 wund（身体创伤），与德语 Wunde 同源；与 wind 的过去式 wound 仅为同形，无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The broken skin comes first, then the act of breaking it, then the doing of it to feelings, and finally to a cause or a bond.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是破开的皮肤，再是打破它的动作，接着是对感情下手，最后到事业或关系上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scab with a red rim around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：结痂却还红着的口子。

branches.en: The injury branch: a wound slow to close.
branches.cn: 伤口分支：迟迟不合的口子。

branches.en: The harm branch: wounded in the shoulder during a match.
branches.cn: 伤害分支：比赛中肩膀受伤。

branches.en: The feeling branch: words that hurt more than accidents.
branches.cn: 情感分支：比事故更刺痛的话。

branches.en: The lasting branch: trust between two towns damaged.
branches.cn: 持久分支：两镇之间受损的信任。

branches.en: The image branch: the body wound gives the feeling the same word.
branches.cn: 形象分支：身体之伤把同一个词给了情感。

intro.en: Wound is a bare stem; -ed and -ing build its forms, and the spelling also belongs to another verb entirely.
intro.cn: wound 是裸词干；-ed 与 -ing 构成其余形式，而这个拼写还属于另一个动词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below name injury and its mark.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词指损伤及其痕迹。

items.example: Its past tense is also wound.
It sounds like the oo in spoon.
items.exampleCN: 读起来像 spoon 里的 oo。

definition_zh: n. 捐赠者；捐款人；供血者；器官捐献者；施主（半导体）
definition_en: a person or organisation that gives money, blood, organs or aid, or an impurity that supplies electrons
core_image: 一张姓名栏空着的支票；冷柜里一排贴着标签的血袋；一张签过名的卡片放在钱包里驾照旁边；一只印着援助机构标记的板条箱；一张晶格图上多余电子被标为自由
scene: 医院收到一张支票，姓名栏空着，只附了一句祝早日康复。 The hospital thanked its anonymous donor.
sceneCN: 这里 donor 是「捐款人」（第 1 个义项：向某事业捐钱的人或机构）；句意：医院感谢了那位匿名捐款人。图中可辨识物件：支票、空白的姓名栏、医院柜台、祝福字条。

pos.zh: 捐赠者；捐款人；供血者；器官捐献者；施主（半导体）

senses.title: A money giver
senses.definition: a person or body that gives money to a cause
senses.definitionCN: （名词）向某事业捐钱的人或机构
senses.example: The hospital thanked its anonymous donor.
senses.exampleCN: 医院感谢了那位匿名捐款人。
senses.why: A cheque with the name line left blank.
senses.whyCN: 一张姓名栏空着的支票。

senses.title: A blood giver
senses.definition: a person who gives blood for medical use
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为医疗用途献血的人
senses.example: The clinic needs donors of the rarest type.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所需要最稀有血型的供血者。
senses.why: A row of labelled bags in a cold cabinet.
senses.whyCN: 冷柜里一排贴着标签的血袋。

senses.title: An organ giver
senses.definition: a person whose organs are used for transplant
senses.definitionCN: （名词）器官被用于移植的人
senses.example: The transplant waited for a matching donor.
senses.exampleCN: 移植手术在等待配型相合的捐献者。
senses.why: A signed card carried in a wallet beside a licence.
senses.whyCN: 一张签过名的卡片放在钱包里、驾照旁边。

senses.title: An aid body
senses.definition: an organisation that supplies goods or aid
senses.definitionCN: （名词）提供物资或援助的机构
senses.example: Several donors funded the new library wing.
senses.exampleCN: 几家捐赠机构资助了图书馆新翼。
senses.why: A crate stamped with the mark of a foreign aid body.
senses.whyCN: 一只印着外国援助机构标记的板条箱。

senses.title: A semiconductor impurity
senses.definition: an impurity that supplies free electrons in a semiconductor
senses.definitionCN: （名词）半导体中提供自由电子的杂质
senses.example: Phosphorus acts as a donor in silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 磷在硅中起施主作用。
senses.why: A lattice diagram with one extra electron marked loose.
senses.whyCN: 一张晶格图，其中一个多余电子被标为自由。

intro.en: Donor is don- plus -or, the one who does; it goes back through Old French doneur to Latin donator, a giver, from donare, to give as a gift.
intro.cn: donor 由 don- 加 -or「做…的人」构成；它经古法语 doneur 追溯到拉丁语 donator「给予者」，源自 donare「作为礼物给予」。

items.en: Latin donum means a gift.
items.cn: 拉丁语 donum 意为礼物。

items.en: Donare means to give as a gift.
items.cn: donare 意为作为礼物给予。

items.en: Donator means a giver.
items.cn: donator 意为给予者。

items.en: Old French doneur names the one who gives.
items.cn: 古法语 doneur 指给予的人。

items.en: The word comes to name blood and organ givers.
items.cn: 这个词转而指血液与器官的给予者。

items.en: Donor also names an impurity supplying electrons.

note.en: Donor is the one who gives; its look-alikes share the gift root, and its neighbours name other givers and the opposite receiver.

dict_mnemonic.text: donor ＝ don（礼物，拉丁语 donum）＋ -or（名词后缀，表示「做…的人」）＝「送礼的人」。与之相对，-ee 表示「受…的人」，所以受赠人是 donee；捐出的东西或行为是 donation，动作本身是 donate。

root: 拉丁语 donum（礼物）→ donare（赠予）→ donator（给予者）→ 古法语 doneur → 英语 donor

sensesIntro.en: The giving hand in five scenes: a blank-name cheque, labelled bags in a cold cabinet, a signed card in a wallet, a stamped aid crate and a loose electron in a lattice.

intro.en: Donor is don- plus -or; -ee marks the receiver in donee, -ate the verb donate and -ation the noun donation, while bene- builds benefactor.

latinIntro.en: Latin donum means a gift, donare to give and donator a giver; bene means well and tribuere to allot.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 donum 意为礼物，donare 意为给予，donator 意为给予者；bene 意为好，tribuere 意为分配。

definition_zh: 接受者；收件人；获奖者；接受移植的人
definition_en: a person or organisation that receives something given, sent or granted
core_image: 一只伸出的手，掌心朝上，等着东西放进来
scene: 信寄到了，收件人那一栏写的是一个早已搬走多年的名字。 The envelope arrived, but the recipient had moved away years before.
sceneCN: 这里 recipient 指收件人（第 1 个义项：信件的接收者）；句意为信寄到了，收件人那一栏写的是一个早已搬走多年的名字。

pos.zh: 接受者；收件人；获奖者；接受者（医疗）

senses.title: The recipient of a letter
senses.definition: the person named to receive a message or parcel
senses.definitionCN: 被指定接收讯息或包裹的人
senses.example: The recipient had moved away years before the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到的时候，收件人已经搬走多年了。
senses.why: The first sense is postal and ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是邮政的、日常的。

senses.title: The recipient of an award
senses.definition: the person on whom a prize or honour is conferred
senses.definitionCN: 被授予奖项或荣誉的人
senses.example: The recipient of the prize gave no speech.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖者没有发表讲话。
senses.why: Ceremony turns the word into an honour.
senses.whyCN: 典礼把这个词变成一份荣誉。

senses.title: A transplant recipient
senses.definition: a patient who receives an organ or tissue from another body
senses.definitionCN: 从另一个身体接受器官或组织的病人
senses.example: The transplant recipient was discharged after nine days.
senses.exampleCN: 接受移植的人在九天之后出院。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for the receiving body.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词指接受的一方身体。

senses.title: The recipient's address
senses.definition: the details that locate the party meant to receive something
senses.definitionCN: 用来定位应当接收某物一方的各项信息
senses.example: A misspelled recipient's address delayed the parcel by a week.
senses.exampleCN: 收件人地址拼错，让包裹晚了一个星期。
senses.why: The word can name a field on a form, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能指表格上的一个字段，而不是一个人。

senses.title: The recipient of aid
senses.definition: a party that takes help rather than giving it
senses.definitionCN: 接受帮助而非给予帮助的一方
senses.example: The fund required every recipient of aid to publish its accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金要求每一个受援者公开账目。
senses.why: The sense carries power: someone must give first.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项带着权力关系：总得有人先给。

senses.title: A passive recipient
senses.definition: a person treated as the object of another's action
senses.definitionCN: 被当作他人行为对象的人
senses.example: He was a passive recipient of advice he never asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那些自己从未索取的劝告的被动接受者。
senses.why: The word can criticise a role, not describe a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能批评一种角色，而不只是描述事实。

senses.title: A recipient country
senses.definition: a state that receives funds, goods or expertise
senses.definitionCN: 接受资金、物资或技术的国家
senses.example: The recipient country insisted the terms were not conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 受援国坚持说那些条款不是条件。
senses.why: Aid language fixes the word to whole states.
senses.whyCN: 援助语言把这个词固定到国家整体上。

senses.title: Versus donor
senses.definition: one who receives, as opposed to one who gives
senses.definitionCN: 接受的一方，与给予的一方相对
senses.example: The donor sets the terms; the recipient signs them.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者定条款，接受者签字。
senses.why: The pair is a single transaction seen from two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词是同一笔交易的两面。

intro.en: Recipient comes from Latin recipiens, the present participle of recipere, 'to take back or receive', from re- and capere, 'to take'.
intro.cn: recipient 来自拉丁语 recipiens，是 recipere（收回、接收）的现在分词，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住。

items.en: Recipere added the sense of taking back or in.
items.cn: recipere 加了「收回、接纳」的意思。

items.en: The participle named the one doing the receiving.
items.cn: 分词命名正在接收的那一方。

items.en: English used recipient for receivers of goods and letters.
items.cn: 英语用 recipient 指货物与信件的接收者。

items.en: Today it covers prizes, organs, aid and data.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖奖项、器官、援助与数据。

note.en: The look-alike group is the receive- family; the near-meaning group separates beneficiary, receiver, addressee and grantee.

definition_zh: 康复；复健；改造；（房屋、生态）修复
definition_en: the process of restoring someone's health, abilities or good standing, or of bringing a damaged place or system back into use
core_image: 一个人在平行杠之间一步步重新学走，治疗师在旁边计数
scene: 这里指「康复」。 After the stroke, months of rehabilitation helped him walk again.
sceneCN: 这里 rehabilitation 指「医学康复」（第 1 个义项：通过训练恢复身体功能）；句意：中风后数月的康复训练帮助他重新行走。图中可辨识物件：平行杠、治疗师、秒表、步行路线标记。

pos.zh: 康复；复健；（罪犯）改造；（房屋、生态）修复

derivatives.zh: 康复性的；有助于复原的
获得能力的过程（较少用）

senses.title: Medical recovery
senses.titleCN: 医学康复：通过训练恢复身体功能
senses.definition: the process of restoring physical function after illness, injury or surgery through therapy and training
senses.definitionCN: 疾病、受伤或手术后通过治疗与训练恢复身体功能的过程
senses.example: After the stroke, months of rehabilitation helped him walk again.
senses.exampleCN: 中风后数月的康复训练帮助他重新行走。
senses.why: The noun joins re- 'again' to habilitare 'make able', from habilis 'apt'; rehabilitation is literally 'making able again'.
senses.whyCN: 该名词把 re-「再次」与 habilitare「使有能力」结合，后者出自 habilis「有能力的」；rehabilitation 字面就是「再次使有能力」。

senses.title: Return to work
senses.titleCN: 职业康复：帮助人重返工作岗位
senses.definition: the process of helping a person return to employment through retraining, adjustments or placement
senses.definitionCN: 通过再培训、岗位调整或安置帮助某人重返工作的过程
senses.example: Vocational rehabilitation retrained him as a dispatcher.
senses.exampleCN: 职业康复把他重新培训成调度员。
senses.why: Ability here is employability: the same 'make able again' is applied to a working role rather than a limb.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力指就业能力：同一个「再次使有能力」被用于工作角色，而非肢体。

senses.title: Prison rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 监狱改造：以教育矫正促使回归社会
senses.definition: the correctional aim of reforming offenders so they can rejoin society
senses.definitionCN: 矫正罪犯、使其能够重返社会的目标与措施
senses.example: The prison's rehabilitation programme offers literacy classes.
senses.exampleCN: 该监狱的改造计划提供识字课程。
senses.why: Corrections borrowed the medical word: a person is treated as needing restoration to social fitness, not merely punishment.
senses.whyCN: 矫正系统借用了医学词汇：人被当作需要恢复社会适应力者，而不只是受惩罚者。

senses.title: Addiction treatment
senses.titleCN: 戒毒戒酒康复：治疗依赖并重建生活
senses.definition: the treatment of drug or alcohol dependence, including detoxification, counselling and relapse prevention
senses.definitionCN: 对药物或酒精依赖的治疗，包括脱毒、咨询与防复发
senses.example: She entered rehabilitation for alcohol dependence.
senses.exampleCN: 她因酒精依赖进入康复治疗。
senses.why: Habituation is treated as a loss of control; rehabilitation aims to restore the person's capacity to live without the substance.
senses.whyCN: 成瘾被视为控制力的丧失；康复旨在恢复人不依赖该物质生活的能力。

senses.title: Post-disaster rebuilding
senses.titleCN: 灾后复原：恢复社区生活条件
senses.definition: the restoration of housing, services and livelihoods after a disaster or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 灾难或冲突之后恢复住房、服务与生计
senses.example: Rehabilitation of the flooded district began before the water fell.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水尚未退去，受灾区的复原工作就已开始。
senses.why: The word extends from bodies to communities: what is made able again is a place and its economy.
senses.whyCN: 词义从身体扩展到社区：被重新赋予能力的是一个地方及其经济。

senses.title: Habitat rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 栖息地修复：让退化生态恢复功能
senses.definition: the restoration of a degraded ecosystem or habitat to a functioning state
senses.definitionCN: 使退化生态系统或栖息地恢复到可运作状态
senses.example: Wetland rehabilitation brought the bird population back.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地修复让鸟类种群回升。
senses.why: Ecology uses the medical frame: a damaged system is nursed back to health rather than replaced.
senses.whyCN: 生态学沿用医学框架：受损系统是被调养回健康，而非被替换。

senses.title: Speech and language therapy
senses.titleCN: 言语康复：恢复说话与理解能力
senses.definition: therapy that helps a person recover speech, language or swallowing after injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人在受伤或患病后恢复言语、语言或吞咽能力的治疗
senses.example: Speech rehabilitation continued weekly for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 言语康复每周进行，持续了一年。
senses.why: This narrows sense 1 to communication: the ability being restored is the capacity to speak and be understood.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 1 个义项的窄化：被恢复的能力是说话并被理解的能力。

senses.title: Building rehabilitation
senses.titleCN: 建筑修复：使旧建筑重新可用
senses.definition: the renovation of an old or damaged building so that it can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 对老旧或受损建筑进行翻修，使其重新可使用
senses.example: The rehabilitation of the warehouse created forty apartments.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库的修复改造造出了四十套公寓。
senses.why: Construction uses the same logic: a structure that lost its capacity is made serviceable again instead of being demolished.
senses.whyCN: 建筑领域沿用同一逻辑：失去使用能力的结构被重新变得可用，而不是被拆除。

intro.en: Rehabilitation comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, built from re- 'again' and habilitare 'to make able', which rests on habilis 'apt, able'. The English noun followed the verb.
intro.cn: rehabilitation 出自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare，由 re-「再次」与 habilitare「使有能力」构成，而后者基于 habilis「合适的、有能力的」。英语名词随后出现。

items.en: Habilis 'apt, handy' comes from habere 'to hold, have'. The ability to do something was pictured as something one holds.
items.cn: habilis「合适的、顺手的」出自 habere「持有、拥有」。做事的能力被想象成手中所持之物。

items.en: Medieval Latin habilitare meant 'to make able, fit, or qualified'. It was used for legal capacity as well as physical fitness.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 habilitare 意为「使有能力、使合格」，既用于法律资格，也用于身体适应能力。

items.en: Adding re- 'again' produced rehabilitare, 'to restore to a former capacity or good standing'. The word appears in medieval legal and medical records.
items.cn: 加 re-「再次」产生 rehabilitare「恢复到原有能力或良好地位」。该词见于中世纪法律与医学记录。

items.en: English rehabilitation appears in the seventeenth century, first in legal restoration of rights and later in medicine.
items.cn: 英语 rehabilitation 于 17 世纪出现，先指法律上恢复权利，后用于医学。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it to vocational training, prison reform, addiction treatment, ecology and building renovation.
items.cn: 20 世纪把它扩展到职业培训、监狱改革、成瘾治疗、生态与建筑翻修。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the precise medieval route through French or Latin is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（中世纪传入路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；经由法语或拉丁的确切中世纪路径也无完整文献可证。

note.en: The first group separates the rehabilitate family; the second gives near-synonyms for recovery, reform and restoration.
note.cn: 第一组区分 rehabilitate 词族；第二组给出关于康复、改造与修复的近义词。

entries.definition: To restore someone's ability or standing. Rehabilitation is the process or programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复某人的能力或地位；rehabilitation 是过程或计划。

entries.definition: Describing treatment or measures that restore ability. It modifies the programme, not names it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容恢复能力的治疗或措施，修饰计划而非命名计划。

entries.definition: The initial process of making someone able, especially in development contexts. Rehabilitation adds the idea of restoring what was lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指最初使某人获得能力的过程，尤见于发展语境；rehabilitation 增加了「恢复已失之物」的意思。

entries.definition: The colloquial shortening for a rehabilitation programme or centre. It is not used in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 计划或中心的口语缩略，不用于正式写作。

entries.definition: A return to health or normal state. It can be spontaneous, while rehabilitation implies a structured programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复健康或正常状态；可以是自然发生的，而 rehabilitation 暗示有组织的计划。

entries.definition: Bringing something back to its earlier condition, often with fidelity. Rehabilitation stresses renewed function more than original form.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复到较早的状态，常强调忠于原貌；rehabilitation 更强调功能恢复而非原貌。

entries.definition: Changing something for the better, especially institutions or behaviour. Prison rehabilitation is one kind of reform.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物变好，尤指制度或行为；监狱改造是改革的一种。

entries.definition: Treatment aimed at healing. Rehabilitation is often delivered through therapy but is the broader programme.
entries.definitionCN: 指以治愈为目标的治疗；rehabilitation 常通过治疗实施，但范围更广。

entries.definition: The process of coming back into a group or society. It is the goal of much rehabilitation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新回到群体或社会的过程；它是许多康复的目标，而非全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + habilis 'able' + -ation: making able again.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ habilis「有能力的」+ -ation：再次使有能力。

normal.en: The family runs rehabilitate, rehabilitative, rehab, habilitate, ability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rehabilitate、rehabilitative、rehab、habilitate、ability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: physical rehabilitation, vocational rehabilitation, prison rehabilitation, habitat rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：身体康复、职业康复、监狱改造、栖息地修复。

normal.en: rehab is the informal short form used for centres and programmes.
normal.cn: rehab 是中心与计划的口语缩略形式。

normal.en: The same word treats a limb, a worker, an offender, an addict, a district, a wetland and an old warehouse.
normal.cn: 同一个词可处理肢体、工人、罪犯、成瘾者、街区、湿地与旧仓库。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on parallel bars, counting each step back to walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶在平行杠上，数着一步步走回行走。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom inside a prison where someone sounds out a first word.
abstract.cn: 想象监狱里的一间教室，有人拼出第一个词。

abstract.en: Picture an old warehouse with its roof patched, its windows lit again.
abstract.cn: 想象一座旧仓库屋顶修补、窗户重新亮起。

examples.en: The rehabilitation unit has a treadmill, a pool and a mock kitchen.
examples.cn: 康复病区配有跑步机、泳池和模拟厨房。

examples.en: Rehabilitation of the mine site will take decades.
examples.cn: 矿区的生态修复需要数十年。

examples.en: The programme combines rehabilitation with job placement.
examples.cn: 该计划把康复训练与就业安置结合起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ ability（能力）」——把能力还给他 → rehabilitation 康复、复健

root: 拉丁 habere「持有」→ habilis「有能力的」→ habilitare「使有能力」→ re + habilitare；英语 rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses restore capacity in different bodies: a patient, a worker, an offender, an addict, a flooded town, a wetland, a speaker, an old building.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同对象上恢复能力：病人、工人、罪犯、成瘾者、受淹城镇、湿地、说话者、旧建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on parallel bars, counting steps back to walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：手扶平行杠，数着走回行走的步子。

branches.en: THE BODY: movement and speech are trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：运动与言语被训练回可用状态。

branches.en: WORK: ability is redefined as employability.
branches.cn: 工作：能力被重新定义为可就业性。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: offenders and addicts are treated as people needing restoration, not only punishment.
branches.cn: 行为：罪犯与成瘾者被当作需要恢复的人，而不只是受惩罚者。

branches.en: PLACES: a district or an ecosystem is nursed back to function.
branches.cn: 地方：街区或生态系统被调养回功能状态。

branches.en: BUILDINGS: an old structure is made serviceable instead of demolished.
branches.cn: 建筑：旧结构被重新变得可用，而非拆除。

intro.en: Rehabilitation is a medieval Latin verb of making-able, turned into a noun of action; re- adds restoration, habilis supplies ability.
intro.cn: rehabilitation 是表示「使有能力」的中世纪拉丁动词转为动作名词；re- 增加「恢复」义，habilis 提供「能力」义。

latinIntro.en: The habere family includes able, ability, habilitate, rehabilitation, habit, exhibit, inhibit and prohibit; the core sense is holding or having.
latinIntro.cn: habere 词族包括 able、ability、habilitate、rehabilitation、habit、exhibit、inhibit、prohibit，核心义是持有或拥有。

items.exampleCN: 膝盖手术后进行了康复训练。

items.meaning: to restore to ability or good standing
items.meaningCN: 使恢复能力或良好地位

items.example: Rehabilitative care began on the second day.
items.exampleCN: 康复护理从第二天开始。

items.example: The course habilitates nurses for rural practice.
items.exampleCN: 该课程使护士具备农村执业能力。

items.example: She regained the ability to write.
items.exampleCN: 她重新获得了书写能力。
这一习惯是多年形成的。

definition_zh: 抑郁；萧条；凹陷
definition_en: a long feeling of sadness, a period of low economic activity, or a hollow in a surface
core_image: 一片凹下去的地面，雨水积在最低处，久久不退
scene: 雨停之后，操场中间积了一小片水，四周都比它高。 The depression of the ground held water for days.
sceneCN: 这里 depression 指「凹陷」（第 3 个义项：表面上凹下去的地方）；句意是地面的凹陷把水留了好几天。

senses.title: A long feeling of sadness
senses.definition: a medical condition or a long period of deep sadness
senses.definitionCN: 一种医学状态或长期的深切悲伤
senses.example: He has struggled with depression for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他与抑郁抗争了多年。
senses.why: Sadness that will not lift becomes an illness with a name.
senses.whyCN: 迟迟不散去的悲伤，成了一种有名字的病。

senses.title: A period of low business
senses.definition: a long period when business is bad and many lose work
senses.definitionCN: 生意低迷、许多人失业的长期时期
senses.example: The depression closed half the shops in town.
senses.exampleCN: 萧条让镇上半数店铺关了门。
senses.why: An economy can sink the way a floor can sink.
senses.whyCN: 经济会下沉，就像地面会下陷。

senses.title: A hollow in a surface
senses.definition: a place where a surface is pressed or worn down
senses.definitionCN: 表面被压下去或磨下去的地方
senses.example: The depression of the ground held water for days.
senses.exampleCN: 地面的凹陷把水留了好几天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a place pressed down.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思，就是一个被压下去的地方。

intro.en: Depression is the Latin noun depressio, from deprimere, to press down.
intro.cn: depression 是拉丁语名词 depressio，来自 deprimere（向下压）。

items.en: Deprimere meant to press down, from de- and premere.
items.cn: deprimere 意为向下压，由 de- 与 premere 组成。

items.en: Depressio named a sinking or a low place.
items.cn: depressio 指下陷或低洼处。

items.en: English used depression for a hollow or a lowering.
items.cn: 英语用 depression 表示凹陷或降低。

items.en: It described low spirits and, later, low trade.
items.cn: 它先形容低落的精神，后来又形容低迷的贸易。

items.en: The Great Depression fixed the economic sense worldwide.
items.cn: 大萧条让经济这一层意思在全世界固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depress stem, and the meaning group gives a mood word, an economic word and a shape word.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depress 词干，近义组则分别给出情绪词、经济词与形状词。

entries.definition: to press down or make low
entries.definitionCN: 按下或使低落

entries.definition: feeling very low
entries.definitionCN: 情绪非常低落的

entries.definition: relating to low mood
entries.definitionCN: 与低落情绪有关的

entries.definition: the feeling of being unhappy
entries.definitionCN: 不快乐的感觉

entries.definition: a period when business shrinks
entries.definitionCN: 商业萎缩的一段时期

entries.definition: an empty space inside something
entries.definitionCN: 某物内部空出的地方

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with rain filling a low patch of ground and end with a shop that closes for good.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从雨水积在低洼处开始，落到一家再也不开门的店。

normal.en: Water finds the lowest place, and so does the word depression.
normal.cn: 水找最低处，depression 这个词也一样。

normal.en: A low economy and a low mood are both called a depression.
normal.cn: 低迷的经济与低落的心情，都叫 depression。

normal.en: A depression in the ground keeps what falls into it.
normal.cn: 地面的凹陷会留住落进去的东西。

normal.en: The Great Depression put the word on every front page.
normal.cn: 大萧条把这个词放上了每一份头版。

normal.en: Depression is the noun behind depress, depressed and depressive.
normal.cn: depression 是 depress、depressed 与 depressive 背后的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow bowl of ground holding a mirror of water.
abstract.cn: 想象地上浅浅一只碗，盛着一面水镜。

abstract.en: Picture a street of shops with shutters down.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街的店铺都拉下了卷帘。

abstract.en: Picture a person sitting in a room with the curtains closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐在拉着窗帘的房间里。

examples.en: He has struggled with depression for years.
examples.cn: 他与抑郁抗争了多年。

examples.en: The depression closed half the shops in town.
examples.cn: 萧条让镇上半数店铺关了门。

examples.en: The depression of the ground held water for days.
examples.cn: 地面的凹陷把水留了好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depression 记成「地压深」：de 向下，press 压，ion 名词尾，地被压出一个深坑，就是凹陷，也指心情的低谷。

root: 来自拉丁语 depressio，源头是 deprimere（向下压）。它最早指地面上的低洼处，十四世纪进入英语；十七世纪起用来形容低落的精神与低迷的商业，二十世纪的大萧条让经济这一层意思传遍世界。

sensesIntro.en: From a hollow that holds rain, to a mood that will not lift, to an economy that will not move.
sensesIntro.cn: 从盛着雨水的凹陷，到迟迟不散的低落，再到迟迟不动经济。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rain gathers in the lowest patch and stays there.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨水聚在最低处，久久不退。

branches.en: The first sense is a mood with no way up.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是找不到出口的心情。

branches.en: The second sense is an economy stuck at a low level.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是卡在低位的经济。

branches.en: The third sense is the oldest: a place pressed below its edges.
branches.cn: 第三个义项最古老：一个低于四周的地方。

branches.en: Both a person and a market can be said to be in a depression.
branches.cn: 人与市场，都可以说陷在 depression 里。

branches.en: A low economy and a low patch of ground share the same picture.
branches.cn: 低迷的经济与低洼的地面，共用同一幅图。

intro.en: Depression is the noun at the centre of the pressing family, from the verb to the medical adjective.
intro.cn: depression 是「压」这一族词中心的名词，从动词一直连到医学形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is premere, to press, with de- meaning down and -ion making a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 premere（压），de- 表示向下，-ion 构成名词。
