to push down or make low
items.example: Do not depress the red switch.

items.meaning: in a way that lowers the mood
a substance that slows the body
a drug that lifts low mood
items.exampleCN: 医生给他换了抗抑郁药。

definition_zh: 焦虑；忧虑；担心；令人焦虑的事；渴望；焦虑状态
definition_en: a feeling of worry and nervousness about something uncertain, or a strong wish to do something
core_image: 胸口被一只看不见的手慢慢收紧，却还找不到要发生的事
scene: 考试前夜，学生一遍遍翻着笔记本，手心全是汗。 Her anxiety before the exam kept her awake until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 anxiety 是「焦虑、忧虑」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事的担心与不安）；句意为考试前的焦虑让她一直清醒到天亮。画面里有台灯、摊开的笔记本和发汗的手。

pos.zh: 名词：焦虑；忧虑；担心；焦虑的事；渴望

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干加 -ious 构成，义为「焦虑的；渴望的」
由 anxious 加 -ly 构成，义为「焦虑地；急切地」
由 anxious 加 -ness 构成，义为「焦虑的状态」
由 anxi- 与希腊语词根构成，义为「抗焦虑的；抗焦虑药」

senses.title: A feeling of worry and unease
senses.definition: a feeling of worry and nervousness about something uncertain that may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对可能发生却又不确定之事感到担心和紧张的情绪
senses.example: The uncertainty about the job left her full of anxiety.
senses.exampleCN: 工作前景的不确定让她满心焦虑。
senses.why: Latin angere meant to squeeze the throat, and the feeling is still a tightening that has no clear object yet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angere 意为「勒紧喉咙」，这种感受至今仍是一种还没有明确对象的收紧。

senses.title: Something that causes worry
senses.definition: a situation, matter, or person that causes worry and unease
senses.definitionCN: 引起担心与不安的处境、事情或人
senses.example: Money was a constant anxiety for the young couple.
senses.exampleCN: 钱的问题一直是这对年轻夫妇的焦虑来源。
senses.why: The feeling can also name its own cause, so the thing that tightens the chest is called an anxiety too.
senses.whyCN: 这种情绪也可以用来称呼它的起因，于是那个让胸口收紧的东西也被叫作焦虑。

senses.title: An eager wish
senses.definition: a strong or eager wish to do something or to have something happen
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而急切地想要做某事或让某事发生的愿望
senses.example: He waited with anxiety for the letter to arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 他急切地等着那封信到来。
senses.why: The same tightening comes from wanting as from fearing: the body cannot tell a hoped-for event from a dreaded one.
senses.whyCN: 「想要」与「害怕」引起的是同一种收紧：身体分不清盼来的事和怕来的事。

senses.title: A clinical anxiety condition
senses.definition: a medical condition marked by persistent, excessive worry that interferes with daily life
senses.definitionCN: 以持续、过度的担忧干扰日常生活为特征的医学状态
senses.example: The clinic treats anxiety as well as depression.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所既治疗焦虑症，也治疗抑郁症。
senses.why: When the tightening never loosens and starts to block ordinary life, the everyday feeling is given a clinical name.
senses.whyCN: 当这种收紧一直不松开，并开始妨碍日常生活，日常情绪就被赋予了一个临床名称。

intro.en: Anxiety comes from Latin, and its oldest image is physical: a throat being squeezed shut.
intro.cn: anxiety 来自拉丁语，它最古老的意象是身体性的：喉咙被掐紧。

items.en: The verb angere meant 'to choke, squeeze, strangle', and also 'to trouble, torment'. It is the same root behind English anger and anguish.
items.cn: 动词 angere 意为「使窒息、挤压、勒住」，也有「使苦恼、折磨」的意思。英语的 anger 与 anguish 同出这个词根。

items.en: Its adjective anxius meant 'troubled, uneasy, anxious', literally 'tightened', keeping the image of a constricted throat.
items.cn: 由它构成的形容词 anxius 意为「不安的、忧虑的」，字面是「被勒紧的」，保留了喉咙收紧的意象。

items.en: The abstract noun anxietas named the state itself: distress, uneasiness, anxiety.
items.cn: 抽象名词 anxietas 直接命名这种状态：痛苦、不安、焦虑。

items.en: English borrowed anxiety from Latin in the sixteenth century, at first mainly in learned and religious writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入 anxiety，最初多用于学术与宗教文字。

items.en: The word splits into two registers today: ordinary worry about uncertain events, and a diagnosed anxiety disorder in medicine.
items.cn: 今天这个词分成两个层面：日常对不确定事件的担忧，以及医学上被诊断的焦虑症。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the anxious family; the near-meaning group gathers words for unease that differ in cause, strength, and whether a doctor would use them.
note.cn: 形近组收 anxious 这一族词；近义组收表示不安的词，起因、强度以及医生是否会使用各有不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning worried, or eagerly wanting something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑的；渴望的」，是本词对应的形容词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a worried or eager manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「焦虑地；急切地」。

entries.definition: A German borrowing meaning a deep, often existential dread; it belongs to the same choking root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自德语的借词，义为「深层的、常带存在意味的恐惧」，同出「勒紧」这一词根。

entries.definition: A state of thinking about problems and possible troubles.
entries.definitionCN: 反复想着问题与可能的麻烦的状态，比 anxiety 更口语、更贴近具体事由。

entries.definition: A feeling of interest mixed with worry about someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 夹杂着关心的担忧，语气比 anxiety 温和，也常指「大家关注的事」。

entries.definition: A mild feeling that something is not right, often without a clear cause.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的「不对劲」感，常无明确原因，强度低于 anxiety。

entries.definition: Fear or worry that something bad will happen, usually with a known object.
entries.definitionCN: 对将要发生坏事的担忧，通常有明确对象，比 anxiety 更接近「预感不妙」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real choking root, its Latin noun, and the frames anxiety actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「勒紧」词根、它的拉丁名词，以及这个词实际出现的句式。

normal.en: angere means to squeeze the throat, so anxiety is a tightened chest that cannot name its cause.
normal.cn: angere 意为勒紧喉咙，所以 anxiety 是一种说不出原因的胸口收紧。

normal.en: Anger, anguish and angst all sit beside anxiety on the same root.
normal.cn: anger、anguish 与 angst 都与 anxiety 同坐在这一个词根上。

normal.en: The everyday frame is anxiety about something or anxiety over a decision.
normal.cn: 日常句式是 anxiety about 某事物，或 anxiety over 某个决定。

normal.en: Anxiety disorder is the clinical use, where the worry does not switch off.
normal.cn: anxiety disorder 是临床用法，指担忧关不掉的状态。

normal.en: The plural anxieties often names several concrete worries at once.
normal.cn: 复数 anxieties 常一次指好几件具体的忧心事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing slowly around a throat before any danger has appeared.
abstract.cn: 想象危险还没出现，一只手已经慢慢收拢在喉咙上。

abstract.en: Picture a smoke alarm that keeps ringing in a room with no fire.
abstract.cn: 想象没有火的房间里，烟雾报警器一直响个不停。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying an unopened envelope all day, afraid to look inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人整天揣着没拆的信，既想看又不敢看。

examples.en: His anxiety about the interview showed in the way he kept straightening his tie.
examples.cn: 他对面试的焦虑，从他不停整理领带的动作里看得出来。

examples.en: The new policy has become a major source of anxiety for small businesses.
examples.cn: 新政策已成为小企业的一大焦虑来源。

examples.en: She felt a strange anxiety to see him again after so many years.
examples.cn: 隔了这么多年，她竟有种想再见到他的急切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安哉提」——心里喊「安哉」，却还是提着一口气：焦虑

root: 拉丁语 angere（勒紧喉咙、使窒息）→ anxius（被勒紧的、不安的）→ anxietas（焦虑状态）。同根词包括 anger、anguish、angst。词义从身体的「收紧」转为心理的「担忧」，再分出医学上的焦虑状态。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses follow the same tightness outward: the unnamed feeling, the thing that causes it, the eager version of it, and the clinical state where it never loosens.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项沿着同一股「收紧」向外走：说不清对象的情绪、引发它的东西、它急切的那一面，以及一直不松开的临床状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a throat tightened by a hand that has not yet found a reason.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掐紧喉咙，却还没找到理由。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: unease with no clear object.
branches.cn: 感受线：还没有明确对象的不安。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: the thing outside that keeps the hand closed.
branches.cn: 起因线：外面那个让手一直收着的东西。

branches.en: THE EAGER LINE: the same tightening produced by wanting instead of fearing.
branches.cn: 急切线：同样的收紧，由「想要」而不是「害怕」造成。

branches.en: THE DIAGNOSIS LINE: the tightening stays on and becomes a medical condition.
branches.cn: 诊断线：收紧不再松开，成为一种医学状态。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE LINE: the inner feeling and the outer cause are named with the same word.
branches.cn: 内外线：内心的感受与外面的起因，用同一个词来称呼。

intro.en: Anxiety keeps a Latin root of squeezing plus the abstract suffix -iety, and its adjective branch adds -ous, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: anxiety 保留表示「挤压」的拉丁词根，加上抽象后缀 -iety；它的形容词分支再加 -ous、-ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is angere, anxius, anxietas, and a later combining form anxio- used in medical words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 angere、anxius、anxietas，以及医学词里后来出现的组合形式 anxio-。

items.example: It is the oldest layer under anxiety.
items.exampleCN: 它是 anxiety 底下最古老的一层。

items.example: It appears in anxius and anxietas.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 anxius 与 anxietas 中。

items.example: It forms anxiety from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁词干构成 anxiety。

items.example: It forms anxiolytic, a drug that loosens anxiety.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 anxiolytic，即放松焦虑的药物。

latinEntries.example: It is the root of the whole family.
It is the direct base of anxious.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anxious 的直接基础。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct source of anxiety.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anxiety 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: It shows the physical image most plainly.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它最直白地显示了那个身体意象。

definition_zh: n. 痴呆；失智症（记忆与思维能力的严重衰退）
definition_en: a serious loss of memory and thinking ability, usually in old age
core_image: 一位老人握着钥匙站在门口，却想不起这扇门通向哪里，日历上的名字被反复描过
scene: 照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。 The centre designed signs for people with dementia.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：dementia 指这一类疾病；句意是照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。

senses.title: Loss of memory
senses.definition: a decline in memory severe enough to disrupt daily life
senses.definitionCN: 严重到影响日常生活的记忆衰退
senses.example: Dementia made the names of her grandchildren slip away.
senses.exampleCN: 痴呆让她记不起孙辈的名字。
senses.why: A key held at a door that no longer feels familiar.
senses.whyCN: 一把握在门口、却不再觉得熟悉的钥匙。

senses.title: Loss of thinking
senses.definition: a decline in judgement, planning and language
senses.definitionCN: 判断、计划与语言能力的衰退
senses.example: The dementia made paying bills impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 痴呆让他无法付账单。
senses.why: A calendar with the same name written over and over.
senses.whyCN: 一本同一个名字被反复描写的日历。

senses.title: A group of diseases
senses.definition: the family of conditions, such as Alzheimer disease, that cause this decline
senses.definitionCN: 导致这种衰退的一类疾病，如阿尔茨海默病
senses.example: The centre designed signs for people with dementia.
senses.exampleCN: 照护中心为痴呆患者设计了标识。
senses.why: A ward where every door carries a picture cue.
senses.whyCN: 一间每扇门都贴着图片提示的病房。

intro.en: Dementia is Latin de-, away, plus mens, mind, plus -ia, a condition: the mind gone away.
intro.cn: dementia 由拉丁语 de-（离开）加 mens（心智）加 -ia（病症）构成：心智离开了。

items.en: Mens meant the mind in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智。

items.en: Dementia meant being out of the mind.
items.cn: dementia 意为失去心智。

items.en: Doctors used dementia for acquired mental loss.
items.cn: 医生用 dementia 指后天获得的心智丧失。

items.en: It became a category distinct from lifelong conditions.
items.cn: 它成为与终身性疾病相区别的一个类别。

items.en: Alzheimer disease was placed under the term.
items.cn: 阿尔茨海默病被归入这个术语之下。

items.en: Dementia is now the standard umbrella term.
items.cn: 如今 dementia 是标准的总称。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ment- mind family; the near-meaning group names other losses of mental function.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ment-（心智）家族；近义组是其他心智功能丧失的说法。

entries.definition: Wildly irrational or agitated.
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂的；狂乱的。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 精神的；智力的。

entries.definition: To speak or write about something briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 提及。

entries.definition: Loss of memory caused by injury or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 失忆症。

entries.definition: A state of being unable to think clearly.
entries.definitionCN: 意识模糊；混乱。

entries.definition: A gradual loss of strength or ability.
entries.definitionCN: 衰退。

normalIntro.en: Dementia is de- away plus ment- mind: the mind has moved away from the person.
normalIntro.cn: dementia 就是 de-（离开）加 ment-（心智）：心智从这个人身上离开了。

normal.en: Ment- means mind, as in mental.
normal.cn: ment- 意为心智，如 mental。

normal.en: De- means away.
normal.cn: de- 表示离开。

normal.en: -ia marks a medical condition.
normal.cn: -ia 表示病症。

normal.en: Dementia is an umbrella, not one disease.
normal.cn: dementia 是总称，不是一种病。

normal.en: Dementia care uses pictures on doors.
normal.cn: 痴呆照护在门上贴图片。

abstract.en: A key held at a door that no longer feels familiar.
abstract.cn: 一把握在门口、却不再觉得熟悉的钥匙。

abstract.en: A calendar with the same name written over and over.
abstract.cn: 一本同一个名字被反复描写的日历。

abstract.en: A ward where every door carries a picture cue.
abstract.cn: 一间每扇门都贴着图片提示的病房。

examples.en: Dementias differ in their early signs.
examples.cn: 各类失智症的早期征兆不同。

examples.en: She has cared for her mother with dementia for years.
examples.cn: 她照护患痴呆的母亲多年。

examples.en: The charity funds dementia research.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构资助痴呆研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: dementia ＝ de-（离开）＋ ment（心智，与 mental 同根）＋ -ia（病症）＝心智离开了，「痴呆、失智症」。

sensesIntro.en: One mind slipping: a name, a bill and a ward of picture cues.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份正在滑落的心智：一个名字、一张账单与一间贴满图片提示的病房。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old person holding a key at a door that no longer feels familiar
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老人握着钥匙站在门口，却不再觉得这扇门熟悉

branches.en: A key held at a door that no longer feels familiar.
branches.cn: 一把握在门口、却不再觉得熟悉的钥匙。

branches.en: A calendar with the same name written over and over.
branches.cn: 一本同一个名字被反复描写的日历。

branches.en: A ward where every door carries a picture cue.
branches.cn: 一间每扇门都贴着图片提示的病房。

branches.en: Both are abilities the mind can no longer hold.
branches.cn: 两者都是心智再也握不住的能力。

branches.en: Both are handled by care rather than by cure.
branches.cn: 两者都靠照护而非治愈来应对。

intro.en: Dementia is de- plus ment-; the mind root builds the mental and memory families.
intro.cn: dementia 由 de- 加 ment- 构成；心智这个词根造出精神与记忆两族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mens means mind, memoria memory and fundere to pour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智，memoria 意为记忆，fundere 意为倒。

definition_zh: 动脉；干线；命脉
definition_en: a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart, or a main route in a transport or supply system
core_image: 一条从心脏出发、管壁厚而有弹性的血管，血液被压着向外流
scene: 医生指着造影图上那条通往心肌的血管，讲它一旦堵住会发生什么。 The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
sceneCN: 这里 artery 指「动脉」（第 1 个义项：把血液从心脏送出的血管）；句意：冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。图中可辨识物件：心脏、冠状动脉、分支血管、血流箭头。

pos.zh: 动脉（把血液从心脏送出的血管）；干线；命脉（比喻主要通道或供应线）

senses.title: Vessel away from the heart
senses.titleCN: 动脉：把血从心脏送出的血管
senses.definition: a thick-walled blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart
senses.definitionCN: 把血液从心脏送出的厚壁血管
senses.example: The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
senses.exampleCN: 冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。
senses.why: Greek arteria first named the windpipe; Galen later showed that these vessels carry blood, and the anatomical sense took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；盖伦后来证明这类管道运送血液，解剖义由此占据主导。

senses.title: A named artery
senses.titleCN: 具名动脉：主动脉、颈动脉、冠状动脉等
senses.definition: one of the large named vessels of the body, such as the aorta or carotid
senses.definitionCN: 体内有专名的大血管，如主动脉或颈动脉
senses.example: The carotid artery was narrowed by plaque.
senses.exampleCN: 颈动脉因斑块而变窄。
senses.why: Anatomy names individual arteries because each supplies a defined region.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学为各条动脉命名，因为每条供应一个确定区域。

senses.title: Oxygen-rich blood
senses.titleCN: 动脉血：含氧较高的血液
senses.definition: in ordinary usage, the oxygenated blood carried by most arteries
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中指大多数动脉所运的含氧血
senses.example: The artery carries bright red, oxygen-rich blood.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉运送鲜红、富氧的血液。
senses.why: Colour and oxygen came to stand for the vessel type, even though the pulmonary artery is the exception.
senses.whyCN: 颜色与含氧量被用来代表血管类型，尽管肺动脉是例外。

senses.title: Arterial disease
senses.titleCN: 动脉病变：硬化、狭窄与阻塞
senses.definition: a condition in which an artery thickens, narrows or blocks, restricting flow
senses.definitionCN: 动脉增厚、变窄或堵塞、限制血流的状况
senses.example: Peripheral artery disease makes walking painful.
senses.exampleCN: 外周动脉疾病使行走疼痛。
senses.why: Pathology attaches the vessel name to the condition, because the disease is defined by where it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 病理学把血管名称附着在病症上，因为这类疾病的定义就取决于它发生在哪里。

senses.title: A transport artery
senses.titleCN: 交通干线：城市或地区的主干道路
senses.definition: a main road or rail line that carries most of the traffic
senses.definitionCN: 承载大部分交通的主干道路或铁路线
senses.example: The new bridge became the city's main artery.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥成了这座城市的主干道。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the bodily image: a trunk route feeds the smaller routes as an artery feeds capillaries.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用身体意象：主干路线像动脉供养毛细血管一样供养小路。

senses.title: An economic lifeline
senses.titleCN: 经济命脉：关键的供应通道
senses.definition: a vital route or channel on which a region's economy depends
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区经济所依赖的关键路线或通道
senses.example: The strait is the artery of regional oil trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海峡是区域石油贸易的命脉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from roads to flows of goods, money or energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从道路扩展到货物、资金或能源的流动。

senses.title: A palpable pulse
senses.titleCN: 动脉搏动：可触摸到的跳动
senses.definition: the rhythmic beat felt where an artery lies near the skin
senses.definitionCN: 动脉靠近皮肤处可以摸到的节律性跳动
senses.example: The nurse felt the pulse in the radial artery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在桡动脉处摸到脉搏。
senses.why: An artery lying near the skin transmits its pressure wave, so the vessel name also names the felt beat.
senses.whyCN: 靠近皮肤的动脉会把压力波传出来，因此血管名称也用来命名可触摸到的跳动。

senses.title: The branching network
senses.titleCN: 动脉分支：越分越细的供血树
senses.definition: the branching tree of arteries that spreads from the heart to the tissues
senses.definitionCN: 从心脏向组织铺开、越分越细的动脉树
senses.example: Each artery divides until it becomes an arteriole.
senses.exampleCN: 每条动脉不断分支，直到变成小动脉。
senses.why: Anatomy describes arteries as a tree, since each trunk divides into ever finer branches.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把动脉描述成一棵树，因为每条主干都不断分成更细的枝。

senses.title: Artery as metaphor for strength
senses.titleCN: 命脉比喻：系统赖以生存的部分
senses.definition: figuratively, the part of a system without which it cannot function
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一个系统赖以运转、不可缺少的部分
senses.example: Young teachers are the artery of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻教师是这所学校的命脉。
senses.why: The image of a trunk feeding the whole body extends to any component a system cannot survive without.
senses.whyCN: 主干供养全身的意象，延伸到任何系统缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery comes from Latin arteria, from Greek arteria, which first named the windpipe. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: artery 出自拉丁 arteria，源于希腊 arteria，后者最初指气管。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek arteria named the windpipe and the air passages. The deeper origin of the word is disputed; one suggestion links ana- 'up' with terein 'to keep', but this is not established.
items.cn: 希腊 arteria 指气管与气道。这个词的更深来源有争议；一种说法把它与 ana-「向上」和 terein「守住」联系起来，但并未确立。

items.en: Galen's anatomical work distinguished arteries from veins and showed that arteries carry blood, not only air, fixing the medical sense.
items.cn: 盖伦的解剖工作把动脉与静脉区分开来，并证明动脉运送的是血而非只有气，从而固定了医学义。

items.en: Latin took arteria directly from Greek and used it for the blood vessels leading from the heart.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 arteria，用来指从心脏引出的血管。

items.en: English artery is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first in translations of medical texts.
items.cn: 英语 artery 记录于 14 世纪，最早见于医学文本的翻译。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward the word was applied to roads, rivers and trade routes that carry the main flow of a system.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，这个词被用于承载系统主流的道路、河流与贸易路线。

items.en: Source uncertainty (root and first date): the Greek etymology of arteria is disputed, and the first English citation is uncertain; any deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：arteria 的希腊语词源有争议，英语最早书证年代存疑；任何更深的印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds the vessel types and same-family words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for a main route or channel.
note.cn: 第一组是血管类型与同族易混词；第二组是「主要通道」的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to arteries, as in arterial blood; it describes, while artery names the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 与动脉有关，如动脉血；它描述性质，artery 则命名血管。

entries.definition: A small artery that leads into capillaries; it is narrower than an artery.
entries.definitionCN: 通向毛细血管的小动脉，比动脉细。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood back to the heart; the artery carries it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把血送回心脏的血管；动脉则把血送出去。

entries.definition: The main artery leaving the heart; it is one particular artery, not a synonym for all arteries.
entries.definitionCN: 离开心脏的主干动脉，是某一条具体动脉，不是所有动脉的同义词。

entries.definition: Any tube carrying blood, including arteries, veins and capillaries.
entries.definitionCN: 任何运血的管道，包括动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

entries.definition: A principal route of a railway or utility network; it matches the figurative sense of artery.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路或公用设施网络的主路线，对应 artery 的比喻义。

entries.definition: A route or link on which survival depends; it stresses necessity rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 生存所依赖的路线或联系，强调必要性而非规模。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or route between regions, often used for transport or wildlife.
entries.definitionCN: 地区之间的狭窄通道，常用于运输或野生动物迁徙。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek arteria first meant windpipe; anatomy later gave it to the blood vessel from the heart.
normal.cn: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；解剖学后来把它给了从心脏引出的血管。

normal.en: The family runs arterial, arteriole, arteritis, arteriosclerosis and endarterectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis、endarterectomy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: coronary artery, carotid artery, pulmonary artery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：冠状动脉、颈动脉、肺动脉。

normal.en: Arteries carry blood away; veins bring it back.
normal.cn: 动脉把血送出，静脉把血送回。

normal.en: A city's main road is called an artery because it feeds the smaller streets.
normal.cn: 城市主干道被称为 artery，因为它供养更小的街道。

abstract.en: Picture a thick elastic pipe leaving a pump and branching into thinner pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象一根有弹性的粗管离开泵，再分叉成更细的管子。

abstract.en: Picture a motorway feeding a whole city of small streets.
abstract.cn: 想象一条高速公路供养整座城市的小街道。

abstract.en: Picture two fingers pressed on a wrist, counting a regular beat.
abstract.cn: 想象两根手指按在手腕上，数着规律的跳动。

examples.en: The surgeon cleared the blocked coronary artery with a stent.
examples.cn: 外科医生用支架打通了堵塞的冠状动脉。

examples.en: The river is the artery of trade for the whole valley.
examples.cn: 这条河是整个河谷的贸易命脉。

examples.en: Arteries thicken and stiffen with age.
examples.cn: 动脉会随年龄增长而增厚、变硬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arter 管道 + y」——从心脏向外送血的管道 → artery 动脉

root: 希腊 arteria「气管；动脉」→ 拉丁 arteria → 英语 artery。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one direction: blood is pushed away from the heart through a thick tube, and that tube becomes a named vessel, a diseased site, a main road, an economic lifeline, a pulse, a branching tree and finally a metaphor for a system's vital part.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个方向展开：血液被从心脏压进一根厚管，而这根管子依次成为具名血管、病变部位、主干道路、经济命脉、可触脉搏、分叉树，最后成为系统命脉的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick elastic tube carrying blood outward from the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根厚而有弹性的管子，把血液从心脏向外送出。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND THE TREE: one artery, its proper name, and the branching network it starts.
branches.cn: 管子与树：一条动脉、它的专名，以及它开启的分叉网络。

branches.en: THE OXYGEN COLOUR: bright red blood came to stand for the vessel type.
branches.cn: 含氧的颜色：鲜红的血被用来代表这类血管。

branches.en: THE BODY'S SIGNALS: disease can be seen in the wall, and health can be felt as a pulse.
branches.cn: 身体的信号：病变可见于管壁，健康可感于脉搏。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR OF ROUTES: roads and trade channels feed a region as arteries feed tissue.
branches.cn: 路线比喻：道路与贸易通道供养一个地区，正如动脉供养组织。

branches.en: THE VITAL PART: any system has a component it cannot live without.
branches.cn: 命脉部分：任何系统都有一个缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery is a Greek noun taken into Latin with little change; its English derivatives are built on the stem arteri-.
intro.cn: artery 是几乎原样进入拉丁语的希腊名词；其英语派生词都建在词干 arteri- 上。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin arteria supply arterial, arteriole, arteritis and arteriosclerosis; the Greek origin is shared, and the deeper root is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语 arteria 提供 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis；其希腊来源是共有的，更深词根有争议。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The artery was cleared with a stent.
items.exampleCN: 这条动脉用支架打通了。

items.example: Giant cell arteritis affects the scalp vessels.
items.exampleCN: 巨细胞动脉炎影响头皮血管。
动脉硬化在数十年间缓慢发展。

items.meaning: surgical removal of plaque from inside an artery
items.meaningCN: 从动脉内壁切除斑块的手术
items.exampleCN: 颈动脉内膜切除术降低中风风险。

items.meaning: a main road in a transport network
items.meaningCN: 交通网络中的主干道路
items.example: The arterial road carries traffic around the city.
items.exampleCN: 这条主干道承载绕城交通。

items.meaning: the main artery from the heart
items.example: The aorta is the body's largest artery.
items.exampleCN: 主动脉是体内最大的动脉。

definition_zh: 静脉；叶脉；矿脉；（言行的）风格，一丝（气质）
definition_en: a tube that carries blood back to the heart, or a narrow streak running through a leaf, through rock, or through a person's manner
core_image: 一根青蓝色细管从指尖蜿蜒回到心脏，同时像叶脉、矿脉那样不断分叉
scene: 这里指「静脉」。 The nurse found a blue vein on the back of his hand and slid the needle in.
sceneCN: 这里 vein 指「皮下可见的静脉」（第 2 个义项：透过皮肤能看到、可用于进针的青蓝色血管）；句意：护士在他手背上找到一根青色的静脉，把针扎了进去。图中可辨识物件：手背、青蓝色血管、输液针、止血带。

pos.zh: 静脉；叶脉；（昆虫）翅脉；矿脉；水脉；（言行的）风格，一丝（气质）

collocations.zh: 以同样的风格；顺着同一思路

senses.title: Blood-return vessel
senses.titleCN: 静脉：把血送回心脏的血管
senses.definition: a tube in the body that carries blood from the organs and tissues back to the heart
senses.definitionCN: 体内把血液从器官与组织送回心脏的血管
senses.example: The surgeon tied off the vein to stop the bleeding.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生结扎了那条静脉来止血。
senses.why: Latin vena named any narrow channel, and anatomy kept it for the channel that returns blood, the counterpart of the artery that sends it out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vena 泛指各种狭窄的通道，解剖学沿用它来指「把血送回」的那条通道，与向外送血的动脉相对。

senses.title: Blue line under the skin
senses.titleCN: 皮下可见的青筋：透过皮肤能看到的静脉
senses.definition: a vein that can be seen as a bluish line through the skin and is commonly used for drawing blood or giving a drip
senses.definitionCN: 透过皮肤呈青蓝色、常用于抽血或输液的静脉
senses.example: The nurse found a blue vein on the back of his hand and slid the needle in.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他手背上找到一根青色的静脉，把针扎了进去。
senses.why: Because veins lie close to the surface and carry dark, oxygen-poor blood, they show through the skin as blue lines, and medicine learned to use them as ready access points.
senses.whyCN: 静脉靠近体表、又携带缺氧的暗色血，因此透过皮肤呈现青蓝色；医学便把它们当作现成的进针口。

senses.title: Leaf vein
senses.titleCN: 叶脉：贯穿叶片、输送水分与养分的脉纹
senses.definition: one of the strands of tissue that run through a leaf and carry water, minerals and sugar
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿叶片、输送水分、矿物质与糖分的条状组织
senses.example: The leaf's veins form a net that carries water to every edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这片叶子的叶脉构成一张网，把水送到每一个边缘。
senses.why: The branching lines of a leaf look exactly like the branching vessels of a body, so botany borrowed the same word for them.
senses.whyCN: 叶片上分叉的线条与体内分叉的血管形状相同，植物学便把同一个词借去指叶脉。

senses.title: Ore seam in rock
senses.titleCN: 矿脉：岩层中呈条带状分布的矿物
senses.definition: a layer or streak of mineral, such as gold or copper, running through surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 金、铜等矿物在周围岩石中呈层状或条带状的分布
senses.example: Miners followed the gold vein deep into the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工顺着金矿脉一路深入山体。
senses.why: A seam of ore is a thin channel of one substance inside another, the same geometry as a blood vessel, and the word was extended to mining in the Middle Ages.
senses.whyCN: 矿脉是一种物质在另一种物质内部形成的细窄通道，与血管的几何形状相同，这个词在中世纪被延伸到采矿业。

senses.title: Underground water channel
senses.titleCN: 水脉：地下汇流的细窄水道
senses.definition: a narrow underground course along which water flows or collects, often sought when digging a well
senses.definitionCN: 地下水流动或聚积的细窄通道，打井时常被寻找
senses.example: The old well was dug where a water vein ran close to the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 那口老井挖在水脉接近地表的地方。
senses.why: Water moving through soil also follows a narrow line, a sense Latin vena already carried alongside the blood-vessel one.
senses.whyCN: 水在土中流动同样沿一条窄线，拉丁 vena 在指血管之外本就带有这个义项。

senses.title: Manner or tone
senses.titleCN: 风格、口吻：延续同一种写法或说法
senses.definition: a particular style or manner of speaking or writing, especially when something continues in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作的特定风格，尤指顺着同一种方式继续
senses.example: She told a few more jokes in the same vein.
senses.exampleCN: 她又讲了几个同一路数的笑话。
senses.why: A vein runs continuously through a body without breaking, so speech that keeps one tone is imagined as one unbroken line of the same material.
senses.whyCN: 静脉在体内连续不断，于是保持同一基调的言语被想象成一条不中断的同质线条。

senses.title: A streak of a quality
senses.titleCN: 一丝（气质）：性格或作品里隐约的一层
senses.definition: a small but noticeable amount of a quality, such as sadness or humour, in a person or a work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一部作品中隐约可辨的一层气质，如忧伤或幽默
senses.example: There is a vein of melancholy in his early poems.
senses.exampleCN: 他的早期诗作里有一丝忧郁。
senses.why: The mining sense supplies the picture: a thin layer of one substance is found inside another, so a thin layer of feeling is found inside a character.
senses.whyCN: 采矿义提供了画面：一种物质以薄层夹在另一种物质里，于是某种情绪也以薄层夹在性格之中。

senses.title: Insect wing vein
senses.titleCN: 翅脉：昆虫翅膀上起支撑作用的脉纹
senses.definition: one of the stiff ribs that support an insect's wing and carry its hemolymph
senses.definitionCN: 支撑昆虫翅膀并输送血淋巴的坚硬脉纹
senses.example: Biologists count the veins in a fly's wing to identify the species.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家数苍蝇翅膀上的翅脉来鉴定物种。
senses.why: Insect wings repeat the branching-tube pattern, and entomology reused the anatomical word for these ribs in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫翅膀重复了分叉管道这一图案，昆虫学在 18 世纪把解剖学的这个词用来指这些脉纹。

intro.en: Vein comes from Latin vena through Old French veine. Latin already used the one word for a blood vessel, a water course and a seam of ore, and English copied all three.
intro.cn: vein 经古法语 veine 来自拉丁 vena。拉丁语本就用同一个词指血管、水道与矿脉，英语把这三层一并继承了下来。

items.en: Latin vena meant a blood vessel, and by extension a channel of water and a seam of metal in the earth; the shared picture is a narrow passage inside a larger body.
items.cn: 拉丁 vena 指血管，并引申为水道与地层中的金属脉；共同的画面是「较大物体内部的一条窄通道」。

items.en: Old French veine carried the anatomical sense into English around the fourteenth century, at first mainly as a medical term.
items.cn: 古法语 veine 大约在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语，起初主要作为医学术语。

items.en: By the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the word was routine in mining and well-digging, where a vein of ore or water was followed like a line on a map.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，这个词在采矿与打井中已很常用，矿脉或水脉被当作地图上的一条线来追踪。

items.en: Naturalists of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries extended vein to the strands of a leaf and later to the ribs of an insect wing, because the shapes are visibly the same.
items.cn: 17、18 世纪的博物学家把 vein 延伸到叶脉，后来又用于昆虫翅脉，因为这些形状肉眼可见地相同。

items.en: The figurative sense 'tone, style, a strain of feeling' appears in the sixteenth century and survives mainly in the fixed phrase in the same vein.
items.cn: 「口吻、风格、一丝情绪」的比喻义出现于 16 世纪，今天主要存活在「同一口吻」这一固定搭配中。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the deeper origin of Latin vena is unknown, and no Indo-European root is generally accepted for it, so none is reconstructed here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：拉丁 vena 的更早来源不明，学界没有公认的印欧词根，此处不作重构。

note.en: The first group holds sound-alikes and close relatives whose spelling or meaning is easily confused; the second holds words for tubes, seams and streaks that overlap with vein.
note.cn: 第一组是同音或形近、容易混淆的词与近亲；第二组是与 vein 语义重叠的「管道、矿层、条痕」类词。

entries.definition: Means 'too proud' or 'useless'; it comes from Latin vanus 'empty', not from vena.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「自负的」或「徒劳的」，来自拉丁 vanus「空的」，与 vena 无关。

entries.definition: A flat blade that shows wind direction, from an Old English word for a banner; unrelated to the blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 指示风向的扁平叶片，来自古英语中表「旗帜」的词，与血管无关。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the veins'; it describes the vessel rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「静脉的」的形容词，描述血管而不命名血管。

entries.definition: A very small vein; the diminutive suffix marks it as narrower than a vein.
entries.definitionCN: 指小静脉；小称后缀表明它比 vein 更细。

entries.definition: A tube that carries blood away from the heart; vein is the return route, so the two are defined by direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管；vein 是回流路线，两者靠方向区分。

entries.definition: The thinnest blood vessel, where exchange happens; veins collect what capillaries have exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 最细的血管，物质交换在此发生；静脉收集毛细血管交换后的血液。

entries.definition: A rich seam of ore in rock, the mining sense of vein without the anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石中富集的矿层，只保留 vein 的采矿义，不含解剖义。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or an element in a character; it overlaps the figurative sense of vein but has no medical use.
entries.definitionCN: 指细长的痕迹或性格中的一种成分，与 vein 的比喻义重叠，但没有医学用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: English took one Latin word, vena, and kept all three of its senses: vessel, ore seam and water course.
normal.cn: 英语只取了拉丁一个词 vena，却把它指血管、矿脉、水脉的三层意思全都保留下来。

normal.en: The family runs vein, venous, venule, venation and intravenous on the same stem.
normal.cn: 同族词 vein、venous、venule、venation、intravenous 共用同一个词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: jugular vein, portal vein, pulmonary vein.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖位置：颈静脉、门静脉、肺静脉。

normal.en: in the same vein keeps the picture of one continuous streak of talk.
normal.cn: 「同一口吻」这一搭配保留了「一条连续不断的话语线条」这一画面。

normal.en: a vein of humour borrows the miner's sense: a thin layer found inside something else.
normal.cn: 「一丝幽默」这一搭配借用了矿工的义项：夹在其他东西里的一薄层。

abstract.en: Picture an underground river that shows itself only as one blue line under the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一条地下河，只在皮肤下露出一条青蓝色的线。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf held up to a lamp, its veins like a map of small rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子对着灯举起，叶脉像一张小河的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a miner following a thin gold line through grey rock.
abstract.cn: 想象矿工沿灰色岩石中的一条细金线向前走。

examples.en: Varicose veins often appear after years of standing at work.
examples.cn: 静脉曲张常常在多年站立工作之后出现。

examples.en: The rock face was cut by a wide white vein of quartz.
examples.cn: 岩壁被一条宽阔的白色石英矿脉切开。

examples.en: He answered in a lighter vein than the earlier interview.
examples.cn: 他回答的口吻比先前那次采访轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vein 与 vain、vane 同音」——同音词要分清：血管是 vein，徒劳是 vain，风向标是 vane → vein 静脉

root: 拉丁 vena「血管；矿脉；水道」→ 古法语 veine → 英语 vein；拉丁 vena 更早来源不明。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one narrow channel: a tube returning blood, the blue line it makes under the skin, the same shape in a leaf, in rock, in water, in a manner of speech, in a streak of character, and in an insect's wing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条窄通道展开：把血送回心脏的管道、它在皮肤下形成的青蓝线，以及它在叶、岩石、水、说话方式、性格层次和昆虫翅膀上的同形延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow channel that branches through a body, a leaf or stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条在身体、叶片或石头中分叉延伸的窄通道。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND ITS BLUE LINE: the anatomical vessel, then the same vessel as it appears through the skin.
branches.cn: 管道与青蓝线：先是解剖学上的血管，再是它透过皮肤显现的样子。

branches.en: NATURAL BRANCHING: leaves and insect wings repeat the same pattern of fine ribs.
branches.cn: 自然分叉：叶片与昆虫翅膀重复了同样的细脉图案。

branches.en: UNDER THE GROUND: ore seams and water courses are followed like lines on a map.
branches.cn: 地面之下：矿脉与水脉被当作地图上的线来追踪。

branches.en: ONE CONTINUOUS TONE: talk that keeps one style is imagined as an unbroken vein.
branches.cn: 一条不断的语调：保持同一风格的言说被想象成一条不中断的脉。

branches.en: A LAYER INSIDE A PERSON: the mining sense becomes a thin layer of feeling in a character.
branches.cn: 人身上的一层：采矿义转化为性格中薄薄的一层情绪。

intro.en: Vein is a bare Latin stem, vena, with almost no affixation in English; its relatives grow by suffixes such as -ous, -ule and intra-.
intro.cn: vein 是裸露的拉丁词干 vena，英语中几乎没有附加词缀；它的同族词靠 -ous、-ule、intra- 等词缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin vena and its adjective venosus, with the diminutive venula, supply the whole English family, including medical compounds built with intra-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vena 及其形容词 venosus、小称 venula 提供了整个英语词族，包括用 intra- 构成的医学复合词。

items.example: The needle went into a vein.
Venous blood returns to the right side of the heart.
A venule drains into a larger vein.
items.exampleCN: 小静脉汇入更大的静脉。

items.meaning: the pattern of veins in a leaf or wing
items.meaningCN: 叶脉或翅脉的分布格局
items.example: The venation of the leaf is net-like.
items.exampleCN: 这片叶子的脉序呈网状。

items.meaning: a small vein of a leaf
items.example: Water reaches the edge along tiny veinlets.
items.exampleCN: 水沿着细小叶脉到达叶缘。

latinEntries.meaning: a blood vessel; a water course; a seam of ore

definition_zh: 肝脏；肝；（可食用的）肝；（旧）过某种生活的人
definition_en: the large organ in the abdomen that cleans the blood and stores energy, its flesh eaten as food, or an old name for a person who lives in a particular way
core_image: 上腹部一块深红褐色的肉，表面带着湿润的光，像一座安静的化工厂
scene: 屠宰后的牲畜被挂上铁钩，屠夫熟练地取出一副暗红的肝脏，摆在案板上。 The butcher cleaned the liver and set it beside the other cuts.
sceneCN: 这里 liver 是「肝脏」（第 1 个义项：体内的脏器，也常指可食用的肝）；句意为屠夫洗净肝脏，放在其他肉块旁边。图中可辨识物件：铁钩、案板、暗红色的肝脏。

collocations.zh: 把它的肝吃掉；喻指被彻底制服

derivatives.zh: 由 liver 加 -ish 构成，义为「肝色的；易怒的」，旧时认为肝气影响脾气
由德语 Leberwurst 借入，liver 对应 Leber，义为「肝泥香肠」
由 liver 与 spot 复合，义为「肝斑」，旧时误以为与肝有关

senses.title: The organ that cleans the blood
senses.definition: the large reddish-brown organ in the abdomen that removes waste from the blood and stores energy
senses.definitionCN: 腹部内那只红褐色的大器官，负责清除血液中的废物并储存能量
senses.example: The liver processes most of the alcohol taken into the body.
senses.exampleCN: 进入体内的酒精大部分由肝脏处理。
senses.why: Old English lifer named this organ in all three Germanic languages, but why a word for life was used is uncertain; the body part is the fixed centre while the reasons behind the name are disputed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lifer 在三种日耳曼语中都用它指这个器官，但为什么用一个与「生命」有关的词来命名则来源不确定；器官本身是固定的核心，命名的原因却存疑。

senses.title: The organ as food
senses.definition: the flesh of an animal's liver eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 供人食用的动物肝脏
senses.example: She fried the liver with onions and served it hot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把肝和洋葱一起煎好，趁热端上桌。
senses.why: A butcher's counter sells the organ as meat, so the same word quietly moves from anatomy to the plate without needing a second term.
senses.whyCN: 肉摊把这只器官当作肉来卖，于是同一个词从解剖学悄悄移到餐盘上，也不需要另造一个词。

senses.title: A person who lives in a certain way
senses.definition: an old or literary way of naming a person according to the life that person leads
senses.definitionCN: 一种旧式或文学化的说法，按一个人所过的生活来称呼他
senses.example: He was a fast liver, spending his nights in the taverns of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个放荡的人，夜夜泡在旧城的酒馆里。
senses.why: Once the body word stood for life itself, it could be attached to the adjective for a kind of life; the organ and the person are joined by the idea of living, though the motive of the original name remains uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个身体词被用来指生活本身，它就能接在表示生活方式的形容词后面；器官与人由「生活」这个概念连在一起，尽管最初命名的动机仍然存疑。

intro.en: Liver is an Old English body word shared by the other Germanic languages, and the reason it carries a sense of life is a matter of debate.
intro.cn: liver 是一个古英语的身体词，其他日耳曼语中也有对应词；它为什么带有「生命」意味，学界仍有争论。

items.en: Lifer appears in Old English medical texts as the name of the organ that breaks down food, and the word is masculine and weak.
items.cn: lifer 见于古英语医学文本，指分解食物的器官，是阳性弱变化名词。

items.en: German Leber and Dutch lever are the same word, and the agreement across the family shows that the body sense is ancient.
items.cn: 德语 Leber 与荷兰语 lever 是同一个词，整个语族的一致表明这个身体义项十分古老。

items.en: The stem looks like the word for life, and OLD ENGLISH LIF is its obvious neighbour, yet scholars have long doubted that the organ was named for life and prefer an earlier unrecorded meaning.
items.cn: 这个词干看起来像「生命」一词，古英语 lif 确实是它显眼的近邻；但学者们早就怀疑这个器官并非由「生命」得名，而更倾向一个更早、未见记载的意思。

items.en: Middle English liber keeps the organ sense and also begins to use the word in the phrase for a person of a certain life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liber 保留了器官义项，也开始把这个词用在表示某类生活者的说法里。

items.en: Modern English keeps the organ and the meat, drops most of the moralising uses, and lets medicine build terms such as liver disease and liver transplant.
items.cn: 现代英语保留器官与食用肉两个义项，淘汰了多数带道德评判的用法，医学则造出肝病、肝移植等术语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives of the Germanic body word and one English derivative; the near-meaning group gathers words for inner organs and for eating them.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的日耳曼同族词与一个英语派生词；近义组收表示内脏以及食用内脏的词。

entries.definition: The German word for the same organ, directly parallel to the English form.
entries.definitionCN: 德语中指同一个器官的词，与英语形式直接对应。

entries.definition: The Dutch word for liver, homographic with the English word for a bar used to lift.
entries.definitionCN: 荷兰语中指肝的词；与英语中表示「杠杆」的 lever 拼写相同。

entries.definition: Suffering from liver trouble, or easily angered.
entries.definitionCN: 有肝病的；易怒的；由 liver 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: A sausage made from liver and spices, from German Leberwurst.
entries.definitionCN: 肝泥香肠；来自德语 Leberwurst。

entries.definition: An organ that filters waste from the blood and makes urine.
entries.definitionCN: 过滤血液并生成尿液的器官。

entries.definition: A part of the body with a particular function, such as the heart or liver.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中具有特定功能的部分，如心脏或肝。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the liver, from Greek hepar, the word for liver.
entries.definitionCN: 肝炎；由希腊语 hepar（肝）加 -itis 构成，属医学用语。

entries.definition: The internal organs of an animal used as food.
entries.definitionCN: 动物内脏；常作食物。

normalIntro.en: The word is an ancient Germanic name for one organ, and its family keeps returning to the living body and what is taken from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老的日耳曼语器官名称，它的同族词反复回到活着的身体以及从中取出的东西。

normal.en: Old English lifer, German Leber and Dutch lever are the same body word, so the spelling changes little across the family.
normal.cn: 古英语 lifer、德语 Leber 与荷兰语 lever 是同一个身体词，拼写在整个语族里变化很小。

normal.en: Liverwurst comes straight from German Leberwurst, where the first part still means liver.
normal.cn: liverwurst 直接来自德语 Leberwurst，其中第一部分仍然表示肝。

normal.en: The word once worked on its own as a name for a living person, which is why old texts speak of a free liver and a fast liver.
normal.cn: 这个词曾经单独用来称呼活人，所以旧文本里才会出现 free liver、fast liver 之类的说法。

normal.en: Medicine attaches the word to nouns and adjectives, giving liver disease, liver failure and liver transplant.
normal.cn: 医学把这个词接在名词和形容词前，造出 liver disease、liver failure 与 liver transplant。

normal.en: A liver is the only internal organ common enough on a plate to have its own butcher counter and its own recipes.
normal.cn: 肝是唯一常见到能摆上肉摊、还有专属菜谱的内脏器官。

abstract.en: One word covers a hidden organ and a visible slice of meat, a reminder that the body is also something we handle.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指藏起来的器官，又指看得见的一片肉，这提醒人：身体也是我们亲手处理的东西。

abstract.en: The old moral sense links the organ to how a person lives, suggesting that eating and behaviour were once spoken of in one breath.
abstract.cn: 旧的道德义项把器官与人的生活方式连在一起，说明饮食与行为曾经被放在同一口气里谈论。

abstract.en: Every language needs a plain word for the organ that quietly cleans the blood, and English has kept its oldest one.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都需要一个朴素的词来指那个默默清理血液的器官，英语一直留着最古老的那个。

examples.en: The liver processes most of the alcohol taken into the body.
examples.cn: 进入体内的酒精大部分由肝脏处理。

examples.en: She fried the liver with onions and served it hot.
examples.cn: 她把肝和洋葱一起煎好，趁热端上桌。

examples.en: Doctors found that his liver had been damaged by the infection.
examples.cn: 医生发现他的肝已被感染损伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里佛」——肝藏在肚子深处，像个不出声的老佛；记住 liver 是肝脏，也是餐桌上的一片肝。

root: 古英语 lifer（肝）；与德语 Leber、荷兰语 lever 同属一个日耳曼语族。词干貌似与「生命」有关，但更早的命名动机来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one organ inside the body; the senses then divide into the organ itself, the same organ sold as meat, and an old name for a person of a certain life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是体内的一只器官；义项由此分成器官本身、当作肉出售的同一只器官，以及旧时按生活方式称呼人的说法。

core.cn: 核心意象：案板上一块暗红的肝，表面仍带着安静的光泽。

branches.cn: 外科医生看着腹部影像

branches.cn: 屠夫把一块暗红的肝放上秤

branches.en: onions sizzling beside slices of liver
branches.cn: 洋葱在肝片旁滋滋作响

branches.en: a steaming plate set down at a family table
branches.cn: 一盘热气腾腾的菜放上餐桌

branches.en: an old tavern keeper laughing at a regular
branches.cn: 旧酒馆老板冲着熟客笑

intro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry in its body sense; it is a Germanic noun, and English builds only derivatives and compounds on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词的身体义项没有拉丁来源；它是一个日耳曼语名词，英语只在这个词基上造派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin iecur means liver, but the two forms do not share a root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 iecur 意为「肝」，但两者并不共用一个词根。

definition_zh: 肺；肺脏；呼吸能力；（城市的）绿肺
definition_en: one of the two organs in the chest used for breathing, the pair taken as the source of breath and voice, or a place imagined as the breathing organ of a city
core_image: 胸腔里两片粉红色的海绵，随着吸气慢慢张开
scene: 体检室里，医生把听诊器贴在少年背部，让他深吸一口气再慢慢吐出。 The doctor listened to her lungs and asked her to breathe in again.
sceneCN: 这里 lung 是「肺」（第 1 个义项：胸腔里用于呼吸的器官）；句意为医生听了听她的两肺，又让她再吸一口气。图中可辨识物件：体检室、听诊器、少年的背部。

由 lung 加 -less 构成，义为「无肺的」

senses.title: The breathing organ in the chest
senses.definition: either of the two soft organs in the chest through which air passes and oxygen enters the blood
senses.definitionCN: 胸腔中两个柔软器官之一，空气经过其中，氧气由此进入血液
senses.example: The doctor listened to her lungs and asked her to breathe in again.
senses.exampleCN: 医生听了听她的两肺，又让她再吸一口气。
senses.why: The word names the organ by what it does with air: a bag inside the chest that fills and empties with every breath.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是按器官「对空气做了什么」来命名的：胸腔里一只随每次呼吸鼓起又排空的袋子。

senses.title: Breath and voice power
senses.definition: the strength of breath that supports a loud sound or long effort, usually spoken of as the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 支撑大声或长时间用力时的那股气息，通常以复数 lungs 表示
senses.example: She sang the last note at the top of her lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 她用尽全身力气唱出了最后一个音。
senses.why: Because a voice is pushed out by air from the lungs, the organ name becomes a way of saying how much breath and force a person has.
senses.whyCN: 声音靠肺里的气推出来，于是器官的名称变成了衡量一个人气息与力气的说法。

senses.title: A green space imagined as a city's lungs
senses.definition: a large park or belt of trees described as the part that freshens the air of a city
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为替城市更新空气的大片公园或林带
senses.example: The old park is called the lungs of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老公园被称为城市的绿肺。
senses.why: A park does for a city what lungs do for a body: it takes in air and gives it back cleaner, so the organ is used as a figure for green space.
senses.whyCN: 公园对城市所做的事，正像肺对身体所做的事：吸入空气再还回更干净的空气，于是这个器官被用作绿地的比喻。

intro.en: Lung is an Old English word of Germanic stock, and it is generally linked to a root meaning light, because the organ is light enough to float.
intro.cn: lung 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语词，一般认为与表示「轻」的词根有关，因为肺轻得能浮在水上。

items.en: Old English lungen names the organ, and its plural already points to the pair inside the chest.
items.cn: 古英语 lungen 就是这个器官的名称，它的复数形式已经指向胸腔里的那对器官。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is generally connected with a root meaning light in weight, because lungs are the lightest organs and float on water; most handbooks accept the link, though it is not certain.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式一般认为与表示「重量轻」的词根有关，因为肺是最轻的器官，能在水上浮起；多数词源手册接受这条联系，但它并非定论。

items.en: German Lunge, Dutch long and Swedish lunga keep the same shape, which is why the word looks so unlike Latin pulmo.
items.cn: 德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long 与瑞典语 lunga 保持同样的形状，所以这个词与拉丁语 pulmo 看起来毫不相干。

items.en: Middle English shortens the form to lunge and lunges, and the plural lungs becomes the usual way to speak of the pair.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短为 lunge 与 lunges，复数 lungs 成为指这一对器官的通常说法。

items.en: Modern English adds two figures: the lungs as the source of a loud voice, and a park described as the lungs of a city.
items.cn: 现代英语添了两个比喻：肺是洪亮声音的来源，而公园被称为城市的肺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plural and the English compounds built on lung; the near-meaning group gathers words for breathing organs and for breath.
note.cn: 形近组收复数形式与由 lung 构成的英语复合词；近义组收表示呼吸器官与气息的词。

entries.definition: The pair of breathing organs in the chest.
entries.definitionCN: lung 的复数，指胸腔里的一对呼吸器官。

entries.definition: The amount of air the lungs can take in at one breath.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lung 加 -ful 构成，义为「满满一口（气）」。

entries.definition: A fish that has an organ working like a lung.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lung 与 fish 复合，义为「肺鱼」。

entries.definition: Having no lungs, as some amphibians do.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lung 加 -less 构成，义为「无肺的」。

entries.definition: The organ fish use to take oxygen from water.
entries.definitionCN: 鳃；鱼在水中取氧的器官，与肺相对。

entries.definition: The tube through which air passes from the throat to the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 气管；连接喉与肺的管道，不是肺本身。

entries.definition: The front part of the body between the neck and the stomach.
entries.definitionCN: 胸部；容纳肺的部位，范围比肺大。

entries.definition: The air taken into and sent out of the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 气息；指进出肺的空气本身，不指器官。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English organ name tied to lightness, and its family keeps returning to air, breath and the power of a voice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语的器官名，与「轻」有关；同族词反复回到空气、气息与声音的力量。

normal.en: Old English lungen named the organ, and every Germanic language keeps a close form: German Lunge, Dutch long, Swedish lunga.
normal.cn: 古英语 lungen 就是这个器官的名字，日耳曼各语都保留着很接近的形式：德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long、瑞典语 lunga。

normal.en: The name is generally tied to the Germanic word for light, because lungs are the lightest organs and float on water.
normal.cn: 这个名字一般认为与日耳曼语中表示「轻」的词有关，因为肺是最轻的器官，能在水上浮起。

normal.en: The plural lungs is the usual form for the pair, which is why at the top of one's lungs means with the force of both.
normal.cn: 指这一对器官时通常用复数 lungs，所以「at the top of one's lungs」意为用尽两肺的力气。

normal.en: Lungful adds -ful: the amount of air the lungs can take in at one breath.
normal.cn: lungful 在 lung 后加 -ful，指两肺一次能吸进的空气量。

normal.en: Lungfish are fish with an organ that works like a lung, so the compound joins two breathing worlds.
normal.cn: lungfish 是拥有类似肺的器官的鱼，这个复合词把两种呼吸方式连在一起。

abstract.en: A lung is a bag that must empty itself before it can fill, which makes breathing a lesson in letting go.
abstract.cn: 肺是一只必须先排空才能鼓起的袋子，于是呼吸本身成了「先放下」的一课。

abstract.en: Calling a park the lungs of a city admits that a city, like a body, cannot live on its own waste air.
abstract.cn: 把公园叫作城市的肺，等于承认城市也像身体一样，不能只靠自己呼出的浊气活着。

abstract.en: The organ named for lightness sits at the centre of the body, holding the air that every other organ depends on.
abstract.cn: 以「轻」命名的器官坐在身体中央，握着其他所有器官都依赖的那口气。

examples.en: The doctor listened to her lungs and asked her to breathe in again.
examples.cn: 医生听了听她的两肺，又让她再吸一口气。

examples.en: Smoking damages the lungs over many years.
examples.cn: 吸烟会在多年间损伤两肺。

examples.en: The old park is called the lungs of the city.
examples.cn: 这座老公园被称为城市的绿肺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「龙」——肺像两条长龙盘在胸腔里，一呼一吸都在动；lung 就是肺。

root: 古英语 lungen 指肺；一般认为与日耳曼语中表示「轻」的词根有关，因为肺是体内最轻的器官，能在水上浮起；德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long 同源；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the organ that takes in air; the senses divide into the organ itself, the breath and voice it supplies, and a green space compared to it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是吸入空气的器官；义项由此分出器官本身、它提供的气息与声音，以及被比作它的绿地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pink sponges inside the chest, opening slowly with each breath in.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸腔里两片粉红色的海绵，随着吸气慢慢张开。

branches.en: two spongy organs opening with a breath
branches.cn: 随一次吸气张开的两片海绵状器官

branches.cn: 听诊器下起伏的胸腔

branches.en: a shout pushed out with full force
branches.cn: 用尽全力推出的一声喊

branches.en: a park marked as green lungs on a map
branches.cn: 地图上被标为绿肺的公园

branches.en: air moving into fine sacs
branches.cn: 空气进入细小的肺泡

intro.en: The word is a single Old English stem; its English family is built with -ful, -less and the compound element fish.
intro.cn: 这个词是单一的古英语词干；它在英语里的同族词由 -ful、-less 以及复合成分 fish 构成。

latinIntro.en: Lung is an Old English word of Germanic origin, related to German Lunge and Dutch long; Latin pulmo means lung but is not a cognate, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: lung 是源自日耳曼语的古英语词，与德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long 相关；拉丁语 pulmo 虽也指肺，但并非同源，因此不列拉丁同族词。
